text: Transport runs in eight parallel towers, the residues of the Clifford clock. At the dimension nearest four (a flagged premise) two towers are sterile, $r = 4$ with no time and $r = 0$ with two (an imported fork): six can hold matter, five dark; the mirror is populated by indifference, the odd four by inference from the observed remainder. The residue is soldered, not algebraic, so the one metric superselects tower charge: exact stability, given the sector decomposition and the wall displacement. The mirror tower is proved a copy of whatever the Standard-Model paper derives: a second Standard Model, one visible share to half a percent, given one orientation. The orientation bit is the chirality of the pure spinor, its two halves in opposite families only at tower dimension a multiple of four, so the odd residues have no bit and asymmetric dark matter is the mirror tower's. The odd towers' symmetric relic needs a coupling rule the series lacks. One geometric rule, a common mass quantum per unit ball of each tower's space, returns the dark matter ratio as $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$ against $5.364 \pm 0.065$ observed, found by fitting, at observation level on three premises; the floor $5.255$ holds for every thickness. The mirror's share is the testable claim, already a quarter above the galactic bound on mirror matter. The same bit is argued to be the arrow of time, given a three-way classification of arrows. Tier C: nine premises and a hypothesis are attacked, refutations costed, every identity script-checked.

title: What we assume
D: democracy of the total mass
text: Every populated tower carries the same total mass $M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ on its de Sitter sphere. This is a democracy of mass, distinct from P4's democracy of the asymmetry, which the odd towers do not carry.

title: Hypothesis (U): equal rank-one eigenvalues at the ceiling
text: \emph{Hypothesis (U)}, that the rank-one eigenvalues of the different sectors coincide at the ceiling, so that the neutrino's Dirac eigenvalue $m_{D}$ there is the common leading-order value, which the top retains and the second-order breaking splits for the down-type and charged-lepton sectors.

title: P1: the single frozen point
text: The descent was one event freezing one $I$ and making one orientation choice: all towers couple to one metric and are oriented, where they can be, by the one Witt flag of that event (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}). The orientation clause is used only on the reversal orbit, where the identification of the flag across the two towers is canonical. \emph{Support:} \cite[Thm.~4.7]{ButlerT6}, \cite[Obs.~7.4]{ButlerT12}; the orientation clause is this paper's. Structural premise.

title: P2: indifference, scoped to sector labels
text:
The descent cannot instantiate uncaused distinctions \cite[Principle~5.4]{ButlerT8}, \cite[\S2]{ButlerT13}: it equates along symmetry orbits and never equates inequivalent components. The residues are inequivalent as soldered algebras (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}) except along the reversal $r \mapsto -r$ (exchanging $2 \leftrightarrow 6$, $1 \leftrightarrow 7$, $3 \leftrightarrow 5$, fixing $0$, $4$), so P2 equates along that orbit only; which of $2$, $6$ is visible is declared indexical. Structural premise.

\emph{Scope: labels, not states.} What P2 equates along the orbit are the sector labels the descent deposits, the superselection labels of the deposited algebra, such as the tower charge (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}); it does not equate thermal states within a selected sector, so it says nothing about the temperatures of the two members of a reversal pair. The deposited mode set is declared finite. In the boundary-mode model of a reversal pair (Hypothesis (B') of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.tower-charge-sector-label-temperature-not}) this scope is well defined: on every finite window the tower charge is a sector label and the temperature ratio $\xi = \beta/\beta'$ is not, so P2 reaches the stored charge and leaves $\xi$ free; a temperature becomes a label, in the disjointness sense, only on an algebra with infinitely many modes in one frequency band, which the finiteness declaration excludes.

title: P3: nearest-dimension representatives
text: Each tower is represented at the dimension nearest four; where two are equally near (the odd residues, three and five), the lower one with a single time, else the higher. \emph{Support:} P1's one metric read as minimality. Structural premise; Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(iii) records the other windows.

title: P4: democracy of the asymmetry over the oriented towers
text: The flag acts on every oriented tower's modes at one strength, $\epsilon_{r} = \epsilon$ per mode (not equal mode counts or masses). A theorem for the mirror (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)), void for the odd residues (Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow}), a premise only on the fork $r = 0$.

title: P5: boundary modes hold entropy, not global charge
text: The ascended boundary mode space stores and returns information \cite[Thm.~11.5, Cor.~11.7]{ButlerT5}, quantified by its deficit theorem \cite[Thm.~9.3]{ButlerT5}, not global charge: Gauss-law charges are returned per tower by discharge (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-schwinger-discharge-charged-hole}), baryon number is returned by no hole in any tower. This is what the imported flux \cite[Assembly~5.4]{ButlerT7} already implies here: a hole emits baryons only once $T_{\mathrm{H}} > m_{p}$, below $M = M_{\mathrm{Pl}}^{2}/8\pi m_{p} \approx 6 \times 10^{36}$ GeV, returning below $10^{-20}$ of a solar-mass progenitor's baryons. Declared premise, decisive for Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

title: CPT covariance of the kinematic structures and of every action
text:
\emph{CPT covariance.} CPT conjugation is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional invariant (T14, Proposition 5.2, its first premise: ``checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add'').

\emph{The conjugation.} CPT conjugation $\phi$ is the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate exchanging the two families of maximal isotropic subspaces (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}). Because of the reversal, $\phi$ is an anti-automorphism of the Clifford algebra.

\emph{Convention (field action).} $\phi$ acts on fields as a symmetry: on a vector field by its vector part, and on a connection $A$ through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, $A \mapsto -\phi(A)$, so that curvature is carried by that automorphism. In this convention $\phi$ acts on fields as $C = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, with $\kappa$ complex conjugation on $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C$: its vector part $-1$ is the rotor $I_{6}$ of the identity component, and the flag conjugate that preserves the frozen point's action is complex conjugation, a real-linear one reversing that action (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}). So CPT conjugation is antilinear on the complexified ambient and on the Fock module, of Wigner's antiunitary type (argued there, not proved).

\emph{Action clause.} For every action functional $S_{\mu}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, the gauge couplings among its parameters $\mu$ included, $S_{\mu} \circ C = S_{\mu}$; in particular $C$ does not move $\mu$.

\emph{What is checked and what is premised.} Checked: the fibre metric, the completion, the pairing on the Fock module, and the frozen point's action, which with every functional of real tensor fields invariant under constant $SO_{0}(2,4)$ satisfies the action clause in this convention by the cited result's clause (5). Premised: the imported gauge sector, spinor and fermion fields, and structures later papers add. For the gauge sector the standard CPT theorem for local Lorentz-invariant actions concerns the antiunitary CPT operator of quantum field theory; that this conjugation realises that operator is argued, not proved, so the gauge sector's invariance ``is imported and carried as a premise''.

title: The flag as datum: the sign of the Witt flag is configuration data
text:
\emph{The flag as datum.} The descent's flag $W$ (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) is the $+i$ eigenspace of an orthogonal complex structure $J$ on $\R^{2,4}$, and its conjugate $\overline W$ is the $+i$ eigenspace of $-J$ (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}, clause (2)). The premise: the sign of $J$ relative to the unit $i$ of the Fock module is configuration data of each solution, planted by the descent, and not part of the kinematic structure. That is, in the terms of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, a configuration $x$ and the configuration with the opposite sign of $J$ have isomorphic kinematic structures and lie in the configuration space of the same family of action functionals $S_{\mu}$; the orientation bit $q(x) = \pm 1$ is a function of the configuration, not of the theory.

\emph{What it is for.} With CPT covariance (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}), whose conjugation exchanges the two signs, it places the orientation bit in clause (I) of the Definition, taking both values on every nonempty solution space, rather than in (K) or (D). It is used by \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} and its restatements \claimref{one-relation.imported-flag-arrow-superselection} and \claimref{one-relation.record-chain-votes-measurement-without-collapse}. Without it the conclusion fails in the way those results state: were the sign kinematic, the bit would be constant on every solution space of the theory carrying it, and the two orientations would be two isomorphic theories rather than two solutions of one.

\emph{What would refute it.} A structure of the framework, or a term of one of its action functionals, that distinguishes $J$ from $-J$ relative to the Fock module's $i$ and is fixed by the descent's kinematics rather than chosen by a solution: for example a proof that the pairing on the Fock module, the completion or the frozen point's data carry a preferred sign of $J$. Such a result would make the orientation bit kinematic or dynamically fixed. No observation tests the premise directly; it is a modelling choice about where the bit lives.

title: R1: equal mass per quantum
text: The quanta of every populated tower carry the same mass $m$.

title: R2: one quantum per unit ball
text: A populated tower whose space has $D$ dimensions ($2$, $3$ or $4$) holds one quantum per unit ball $\B^{D}$ of that space, in one unit of length common to all towers: every tower has the same Wigner-Seitz radius. The rule presupposes that all six towers are populated, which for the odd four is the inference of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}.

title: R3: one cell per unshared direction
text: In the sourcing rule, a tower's matter counts through exactly one cell radius of each direction its neighbour lacks, on one side: a five-dimensional tower's matter through one radius of its extra direction, and a three-dimensional tower's sheets stacked one radius apart along the direction it lacks. the section ``The thickness: a contact mechanism'' gives a mechanism that returns this value and costs it.

title: The rate model's kinematic inputs: (L), (U), (C), (I)
text:
\leavevmode
\begin{itemize}
\item[(L)] \emph{Localisation, derived in part.} By \cite[Thm.~4.4, Cor.~4.5, Thms 8.7, 8.12]{ButlerT4} and Step 4a, the completion installs q-number degrees of freedom exactly where division fails, which licenses the window mode space $L(t)$ inside the closure of the degenerate locus; the radiation $R(t)$ is a q-number sector on the model's own grounds, its quanta being the emitted modes carried off $E$ by the emission rather than outputs of the localisation theorems; and that these two exhaust the sectors is the model's exhaustiveness postulate. The total state space at each stage is $H_{L(t)} \otimes H_{R(t)}$.
\item[(U)] \emph{Purity.} The ascended description is globally pure, as in Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality}(i), each step of the evolution unitary.
\item[(C)] \emph{Capacity.} $\dim H_{L(t)} = 2^{|W(t)|}$ exactly, the number $|W(t)|$ of window modes filling to the mode count $N_{\mathrm{6a}}$ of Step 6a and non-increasing thereafter; the Page reading $C(t) \approx S_{\mathrm{BH}}(M(t))$ is for the full window.
\item[(I)] \emph{Injection.} The $k$-th emitted quantum enters in a thermofield pair $c_k|00\rangle + s_k|11\rangle$ with a fresh window mode, the pair form and the marginals from Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent} and Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}; its \emph{freshness}, the clause that the pair arrives uncorrelated with everything already present, comes from neither cited result (Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}(3) leaves exactly such correlations free) and is an independent assumption of the rate model, marked as such precisely as (L$_E$)'s never-return clause is. The quantum carries the marginal entropy $h_k := H(c_k^{2}) \leq \ln 2$, with $H(p) := -p\ln p - (1-p)\ln(1-p)$ the binary entropy in nats and equality exactly at the maximally entangled pair $c_k = s_k$; the thermal accumulation is $\Sth(t) := \sum_{k \leq t} h_k$.
\end{itemize}

title: Introduction
Introduction
text:
The tower paper of this series proves that the (1,1) ascent preserves the signature residue $p - q$ modulo eight, so the transport construction runs in eight parallel towers, one per residue of the real Clifford clock \cite{ButlerT3}. Applied to the matter that gravitates and does not shine, the towers give the mirror's share of it by theorem, prove that the other four shares cannot be derived from the series as it stands, and then, by one geometric rule on three premises of its own, return the whole ratio as a closed form, $(11\pi + 16)/(3\pi) = 5.364$, found by fitting. The paper's level is Tier C: nine premises and a hypothesis, each stated before use, attacked in its own section and carried with its cost, and a falsifiability section that says how each claim would be refuted.

The chain, in outline. A residue fixes no signature, so one must be chosen for each; at the dimension nearest four (Premise P3, with the census of what other choices give) a residue has a single time when the chosen signature has exactly one timelike direction, and two residues fail, $r = 0$ with two times and $r = 4$ with none, the fixed points of the mirror map. Six towers can hold matter, this one and five dark; that they do is a theorem for the mirror (indifference along the reversal orbit) and an inference from the observed remainder for the odd four, since the framework has no other dark candidate (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). The flag does not refine the sort (Witt's theorem), so the $r = 0$ exclusion rests on a two-time import alone, carried as a fork. The five are dark by superselection: the residue is an invariant of the algebra soldered to the metric, not of the algebra alone ($\Cl(1,3)$ and the sterile tower's $\Cl(0,4)$ are the same algebra, $\Mat(2, \mathbb{H})$), so no operator built from the one metric changes residue, and given the sector decomposition the towers are exactly stable, touching this one only by weight. The descent's one orientation, the flag bit, is the chirality of the pure spinor, and its two halves lie in opposite families only when the tower's dimension is a multiple of four: the odd residues cannot be oriented, the even ones can at their P3 representatives, and the asymmetric dark matter is the mirror tower's alone.

Of the five dark towers this paper derives the contribution of one, the mirror's, by theorem, and gives the other four by a rule:
\begin{gather*}
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; \underbrace{1}_{\text{mirror, derived, to half a percent}} \;+\; \underbrace{2 \cdot \frac{4}{3} + 2 \cdot \frac{8}{3\pi}}_{\text{four odd towers, the unit-ball rule, fitted}} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.364,\\[6pt]
\text{against the survey's}\quad
\frac{\Omega_{c}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; 5.364 \pm 0.065.
\end{gather*}
The first term is a theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-assembled}). Everything the Standard-Model paper builds this tower's content from is invariant under the signature reversal that carries $(1,3)$ to the mirror's $(3,1)$, so the mirror tower is a second Standard Model, a massless mirror photon and mirror neutrinos included; with P2 its share is one to half a percent (the half percent is the mean mass per baryon of a helium mirror), at any mirror temperature, because the stored asymmetry is a charge of the descent and not a thermal number. The share is exact and fragile (one flavour's difference at the ceiling would move it by a factor between $4.89$ and $21.4$), and it is already at the edge of the record's bound on dissipative dark matter.

The second term is not derived: the odd towers carry no asymmetry (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}), and a symmetric relic's density needs a coupling rule the series does not supply (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}). What the paper offers instead is the unit-ball rule of the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule'': every populated tower holds one quantum of a common mass per unit ball of its own space, in one common unit, and its matter enters the one metric per unit of our volume through one cell radius of each direction its neighbour lacks. A tower's share is then the ratio of unit-ball volumes $V_{3}/V_{D}$: $\tfrac{4}{3}$ for each three-dimensional tower, $\tfrac{8}{3\pi}$ for each five-dimensional one.

The rule rests on three premises the series does not supply, and it was found by fitting. Its one length, the thickness of the direction we cannot see, is a premise; a contact mechanism returns its value from four clauses on how cells meet a world, each with an alternative the observation excludes, and that mechanism explains the value without deriving it. With the thickness left as a parameter the total has a floor at $5.255$, the family's one prediction independent of it, and meets the observed value at one unit and at $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ units, the chord and the arc of a quarter turn of the nested spheres. The series' one length, the de Sitter radius, makes the spheres physical, but its reductions give totals of $5$, $5.67$ or $4.33$; the inverse-square law shows the thickness is not a gravitational quantity; and the three-dimensional towers' sheets, which momentum conservation displaces with the matter, respond to gravity in full, so that a Boltzmann computation returns the standard model's linear spectra for the rule's composition. All of this is at observation level with each cost stated (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress}), and it changes nothing derived.

The rest of the paper: a projection lemma makes every tower's content dilute as this tower's does; the radiation audit closes the three-dimensional towers by theorem plus Polyakov and leaves the mirror (whose cost is a seeded temperature below $0.448$ of ours) and the five-dimensional towers as open channels; the orientation is shown to be the arrow itself (the seventeenth refutation); infall through this tower's horizons is routed through parallel boundary mode spaces at one wall; and the rung scale is valued conditionally at $3.5 \times 10^{11}$ to $6 \times 10^{14}$ GeV. The exposures are five species, gravity-only coupling, composite self-interaction in the three-dimensional towers, which the galaxy-cluster simulations exclude unless their matter is collisionless, dissipative mirror matter against the dark-disk and collisional-fraction bounds, dark neutron-star mergers with our tidal deformability and no counterpart, permanent direct-detection nulls, and a dimmed final burst for evaporating black holes; the section ``The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper'' collects every prediction in one table.

title: Gravity-only coupling at first order, restated from the acoustic no-go
text: Under the entropy paper's Indifference premise (for the sphere step of the four-dimensional lift) and, wherever the thermal state is used, the singularity paper's premise (Q), and with the other hypotheses the acoustic chain carries: within the s-wave current algebra and its assembled four-dimensional lift, every gauge-charged or charge-conjugation-odd probe has zero linear overlap with the graviton mode, so at first order only the charge-conjugation-even neutral sector couples; in the conformal vacuum its overlap is carried by $T$ alone, and Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.conclusion-does-not-depend-ontology-level} reads it as the one coupling sector, stress-energy (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip}, Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}). Hence matter that gravitates on this metric and carries no gauge charge shared with us acts on us, through the metric-forming correlations, by its stress-energy alone, at first order. With Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}, which makes these correlations its only contact with us, it does nothing else observable at first order. \emph{Provenance:} the series' acoustic no-go \cite[\S5]{ButlerT10} restated, at its mixed level.
proof:
Restatement of the series' own result; no new step. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} shows, for any state invariant under the gauge group, charge conjugation and the modular flow, that a gauge-charged or charge-conjugation-odd probe $O$ has $\varphi(T\,O) = 0$ for the graviton mode $T$ and all its modes $T_{n}$; the induced thermal state has the three invariances under premise (Q), and the conformal vacuum has them without it. At first order, therefore, only the charge-conjugation-even neutral subalgebra couples. In the conformal vacuum the orthogonality of quasi-primaries of unequal dimension leaves $T$ as the only quasi-primary with nonzero overlap, so the coupling is carried by $T$ alone; in the thermal state the first-order coupling sector is the whole charge-conjugation-even neutral subalgebra, generated by the current bilinears and strictly larger than the conformal family of $T$, as that proposition states. Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised} carries the orthogonality to the four-dimensional lift, its sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and its near-horizon reduction at assembly level. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.conclusion-does-not-depend-ontology-level} reads the result as one coupling sector, stress-energy, with no selective coupling, no enhanced source and no enhanced detector, at first order; the statement adopts that reading at the source's mixed level.

Matter of a sector that shares no gauge charge with ours enters our sector's observables through the metric-forming correlations by the linear overlap of its operators with ours on those correlations; by the three results the first-order overlap with the graviton mode is that of the sector just described, so this matter acts on us through these correlations by its stress-energy alone, at first order. Whether the sector touches ours by any other route is not decided by the acoustic chain: "carries no gauge charge shared with us" does not by itself exclude, for example, a gauge-singlet portal. That the metric-forming correlations are its only contact is Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}, assumed here, and the closing clause of the statement is conditional on it; P1 also enters the dark-matter paper's superselection theorem as an assumption there. Every premise of the three cited results is a premise of this one, and reaches its dependants through them.

title: The Witt flag
text: On a rung's hyperbolic plane $H_k$ with null pair $(v_k, w_k)$, a \emph{flag} chooses one null line as the annihilated half; $v_k \leftrightarrow w_k$ exchanges the two. title: Towers, residues, and the flag filter
Towers are residues, and the single-clock filter
text:
The residue $r = p - q \pmod 8$ is invariant along every tower: the eight parallel towers are the eight residues, their parallelism derived rather than described. Call a signature $(p,q)$ \emph{causal} if $\min(p,q) = 1$: exactly one direction of the minority sign, the timelike one, whichever sign convention carries time. Labelling this world $(1,3)$, residue $6$, fixes the convention time $=$ plus, and the mirror residue $2$ reads $(3,1)$; under the opposite convention the two labels swap and the causal sort is unchanged, but every attribution of a Clifford type to a member of the reversal pair passes to the other member, since $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat(2,\mathbb{H})$ and $\Cl(3,1) \cong \Mat(4,\R)$ are not isomorphic. That attribution is fixed by a labelling convention Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} declares indexical, and is so read below. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Census; proved.)} Every residue contains causal signatures once the dimension is free: the lowest are $(1,1)$ at $r = 0$, $(2,1)$ at $r = 1$, $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, $(4,1)$ at $r = 3$, $(1,5)$ or $(5,1)$ at $r = 4$, $(1,4)$ at $r = 5$, $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, $(1,2)$ at $r = 7$. The residue alone therefore sorts nothing; a representative must be chosen.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The sort under P3; proved given the premise.)} Under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} the representatives are $(1,3)$ at $r = 6$, this world; $(3,1)$ at $r = 2$, a mirror Minkowski with real (Majorana-type) spinors; $(2,2)$ at $r = 0$, two times; $(4,0)$ or $(0,4)$ at $r = 4$, none; $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$ at $r = 1, 7$, three-dimensional; $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ at $r = 3, 5$, five-dimensional. Exactly two are sterile, $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ (a figure of the original), and they are the fixed points of the mirror map $r \mapsto -r$: under P3 the towers without a single time are the towers that are their own mirrors.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Sensitivity; proved.)} The sterile set is a function of the window. With any dimension up to five allowed, only $r = 4$ is sterile ($(1,1)$ is a causal signature for $r = 0$); with dimensions three to six, only $r = 0$ ($(1,5)$ is one for $r = 4$); with the upper bound removed, nothing is ($(1,9)$ is one for $r = 0$ at ten); and the literal lowest-dimensional representative of every residue, with no lower bound, is definite for $r = 6$ itself, namely $(0,2)$: without a lower bound the criterion would sterilise this world.
\end{enumerate}
Six admit matter: this one and five dark. Which of the six the descent populated is a further question, answered for the mirror by P2 and for the odd towers only by the record (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}). Structural level given P3; the two-time exclusion at $r = 0$ imports the standard instability of two-time dynamics, flagged, and the flag does not remove it (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}).
proof:
Invariance: the ascent adjoins one plus and one minus, fixing $p - q$; periodicity is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}. (i): $(1,s)$ has residue $1 - s$, so every residue has a causal signature; the lowest per residue is the script's exhaustive census over all signatures of dimension at most ten. (ii): P3 (\claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives}) fixes the dimension at four for the even residues, where the signatures are $(2,2)$, $(3,1)$, $(1,3)$, $(4,0)$, $(0,4)$ with residues $0, 2, 6, 4, 4$, of which the first has $\min = 2$ and the last two $\min = 0$; for the odd residues the candidates at dimension three are $(2,1)$, $(1,2)$, $(3,0)$, $(0,3)$ with residues $1, 7, 3, 5$, the first two causal and the last two definite, so P3 sends $r = 3, 5$ to dimension five, where $(4,1)$ and $(1,4)$ have residues $3, 5$ and are causal. The fixed points of $r \mapsto -r \pmod 8$ are $\{0, 4\}$, arithmetic. (iii) is the same census restricted to each window, script-run. The count: eight minus two sterile is six populated; minus this one is five dark.

The labelling convention used throughout, this world as $(1,3)$ at residue $6$, is read as indexical under \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}, which declares which of $2$, $6$ is visible indexical.

title: The flag is insensitive to the residue: no flag-level strengthening
text: The sterile towers are not the unflaggable ones, and no flag-level strengthening of the count exists: in every nondefinite representative the isometry group acts transitively on hyperbolic planes and on the null lines within them (Witt's theorem), so no representative offers a distinguished plane or half of one, and the descent's flag is as uncaused in $(1,3)$ as in $(2,2)$. The definite representatives of $r = 4$ contain no hyperbolic plane, so no \emph{rung-level} flag can be chosen in them, but the descent's flag, a maximal isotropic of the complexified ambient, exists there as for every even residue (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}); the sterility of $r = 4$ is the single-clock filter restated. So the exclusion of $r = 0$ rests on the two-time instability import alone, and a stabilisation of two-time dynamics is an open fork: six causal towers, the $r = 0$ tower an \emph{oriented} one (Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow}), a Kleinian copy of the Standard Model with an asymmetric share of one, costed in the section ``The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper''.
proof: A hyperbolic plane requires one plus and one minus among the representative's directions, and a definite signature has none. Otherwise Witt's theorem (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-extension}) extends any isometry between nondegenerate subspaces to the whole space; two hyperbolic planes are isometric, so the isometry group is transitive on them, and composing with the isometry of a plane that exchanges its null lines gives transitivity on null lines. In $(1,3)$ the rotation $e_{1} \mapsto e_{2}$, $e_{2} \mapsto -e_{1}$ fixes $e_{0}$ and its orientation and carries $\mathrm{span}(e_{0}, e_{1})$ onto $\mathrm{span}(e_{0}, e_{2})$ and $\R(e_{0} + e_{1})$ onto $\R(e_{0} + e_{2})$: the time orientation distinguishes a time direction, not a plane or a null line, the candidate flags through a time axis forming the celestial sphere. In $(2,2)$ the totally isotropic planes form a one-parameter family per component and the hyperbolic planes a four-parameter family, likewise permuted transitively. The script checks the witnesses and the Jacobian rank exactly. The obstruction is the same in every nondefinite residue, so it cannot sterilise $r = 0$ while leaving $r = 6$ causal.

title: Spinor module and type
text: For a representative $\Cl(p,q)$ let $S$ be an irreducible real module (a real spinor space), and let $D = \End_{\Cl(p,q)}(S)$ be its commutant, a real division algebra by Schur's lemma. Its \emph{type} is $D \in \{\R, \C, \mathbb{H}\}$ together with the number of inequivalent irreducible modules (one or two). The \emph{intrinsic group} of $S$ is the group of $D$-unitary automorphisms of $S$ commuting with the Clifford action, $U(1, D) = \{d \in D : d\bar{d} = 1\}$: $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, $U(1)$ or $Sp(1)$.

title: Type by residue, and what each tower can carry intrinsically
proof:
$\Cl(p,q)$ is semisimple, so it is $\Mat(m, D)$ or $\Mat(m, D) \oplus \Mat(m, D)$, and the commutant of an irreducible module is $D$. The centre is $\R$ when $n = p + q$ is even and $\R[\omega]$ when $n$ is odd, $\omega = e_{1} \cdots e_{n}$ the volume element, with $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}(-1)^{q}$; so two components ($\omega^{2} = +1$) or a complex centre ($\omega^{2} = -1$) according to $n$ and $q$, which depend on $r$ as stated. For the division algebra, Lounesto's construction gives a primitive idempotent
\[
f \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{k}\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(1 + e_{T_{i}}\bigr)
\]
from a maximal set of $k$ commuting basis blades squaring to $+1$ generating a group of order $2^{k}$, and then $f\,\Cl(p,q)\,f \cong D$, of real dimension $1$, $2$ or $4$. Bott periodicity in the form $\Cl(p+1, q+1) \cong \Mat(2, \Cl(p,q))$ (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}) preserves $D$ and the component count, so both depend on the residue alone; the dependence within one period is the classical table (Cartan, Bott), recomputed here: the script builds every $\Cl(p,q)$ of dimension at most five in \texttt{GA.py}, computes the centre by exact linear algebra, finds a primitive idempotent by exhaustive search over blade sets and computes $\dim_{\R} f\,\Cl(p,q)\,f$ by exact rank, agreeing with the table on all twenty signatures and on the eight P3 representatives. The intrinsic group is the unit group of $D$: $\{\pm 1\}$, $U(1)$, $Sp(1)$. (i) to (iv) read off the table, in the labelling convention of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}; the two-sphere in (iii) is the set of imaginary unit quaternions.

title: The residue is a soldered invariant, not an algebraic one
proof: (i): the quadratic form $v \mapsto v^{2}$ on $V$ is intrinsic to $(A, V)$, an isomorphism carrying $V$ to $V'$ carries it to the quadratic form of $V'$, and signature is an invariant of real quadratic forms (Sylvester, \claimref{std-algebra.sylvester-inertia}). (ii): the abstract isomorphisms are the classical table (\claimref{primer.classification-real-clifford-algebras}) (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can} recomputes their invariants: same dimension, centre, division algebra, component count and module dimension for each pair); that none carries $V$ to $V'$ is (i) applied to the differing signatures, and is exhibited directly for the pair $(1,3)$, $(0,4)$: every vector of $\Cl(0,4)$ squares to $-|v|^{2} \leq 0$ while $e_{0} \in \Cl(1,3)$ squares to $+1$, so the image of $e_{0}$ under any isomorphism is not a vector. The script verifies the agreement of the abstract invariants for the three pairs and the sign statements on sampled rational vectors.

title: Frozen-phase operators
text: Two things are fixed, and they are different. The one gravitational metric is shared by every tower (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}); each tower $r$ has its own soldering $V_{r}$, the generating subspace of its own algebra $(A_{r}, V_{r})$, with $V_{6}$ the one metric's tangent space and the others the other towers' (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}). The \emph{frozen-phase sector decomposition} is the hypothesis that the frozen phase's state space is the direct sum over residues of sectors, the $r$-th a module over the soldered algebra $(A_{r}, V_{r})$, and that a \emph{frozen-phase local operator} is a section of one tower's soldered Clifford bundle: built, fibrewise, from that tower's soldering by Clifford multiplication and the connection it defines, with gravity entering every sector only through the shared metric's stress-energy coupling. This is the operational reading of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}, stated as a hypothesis and carried as one.

title: Where the flag is defined, and what it carries
text: Every tower has rungs, the $(1,1)$ ascent adjoining a hyperbolic plane at each floor (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so at tower level every residue is flaggable (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) and flaggability selects nothing. The flag counts no towers; it orients them (the section ``The arrow counted''), and it equips them: a flag on $H_{k}$ is equivalently the complex structure $J_{k}$ on the complexification $H_{k} \oplus I_4H_{k}$ (the plane $H_{k} \otimes \C$, with the field theory's imaginary unit $I_4$, which commutes with every vector of the plane) whose $-I_4$ eigenline is the annihilated half (it lives in the complexification, since no real endomorphism squaring to $-1$ has the two real null lines as eigenlines), and the ladder pair's number operator generates a $U(1)$ commuting with the rest of the rung. So every flagged tower carries rung-level abelian charges, one per rung, whatever its ground type, as this tower's derived content acquires its $U(1)$ from three ladder pairs \cite{ButlerT12}.

title: Null blades, the Fock ideal, and chirality
text: Let $V_{\C}$ be the complexified ambient of a representative, of dimension $2m$ or $2m + 1$, and let $V_{\C} = W \oplus W'$ ($\oplus\, \C\ell$ in odd dimension) be a Witt decomposition into a maximal isotropic subspace $W$ and a dual isotropic complement $W'$, with null bases $w_{1}, \ldots, w_{m}$ of $W$ and $v_{1}, \ldots, v_{m}$ of $W'$ normalised so that $v_{i}w_{j} + w_{j}v_{i} = \delta_{ij}$, and, in odd dimension, an extra unit generator $\ell$ orthogonal to both. The \emph{null blade} of $W$ is $f = w_{1}w_{2}\cdots w_{m}$, and it is annihilated by $W$ from the left: $wf = 0$ for every $w \in W$. The \emph{pseudoscalar} is $I = e_{1}\cdots e_{\dim V}$ for an orthonormal basis, normalised by a fourth root of unity so that $I^{2} = 1$ (the sign of $I$ is a convention; only ratios of its eigenvalues are used below); in even dimension it anticommutes with every vector, in odd dimension it is central. The \emph{Fock ideal} is, in even dimension, the left ideal $S = \Cl(V_{\C})\,f$, spanned by the $2^{m}$ states $v_{i_{1}}\cdots v_{i_{k}}f$ ($i_{1} < \cdots < i_{k}$), the \emph{Fock grade}-$k$ states (counting creation operators, not the Clifford grade); it is the spinor module. In odd dimension the left ideal $\Cl(V_{\C})\,f$ has dimension $2^{m+1}$ and is the sum of the two irreducible modules; the Fock ideal is then either chirality-projected half, $S_{\pm} = \tfrac{1}{2}(1 \pm I)\,\Cl(V_{\C})\,f$, of dimension $2^{m}$, graded by the Fock grade of the projected states $\tfrac{1}{2}(1 \pm I)\,v_{i_{1}}\cdots v_{i_{k}}f$, on which $I$ acts as $\pm 1$ and the extra generator $\ell$ acts as that grade's parity up to a fixed scalar. A state $\psi \in S$ with $I\psi = \pm\psi$ has \emph{chirality} $\pm 1$. For a maximal isotropic subspace $U \subset V_{\C}$, a \emph{pure spinor of $U$} is a nonzero $\psi_{U} \in S$ with $U\psi_{U} = 0$.

title: The two families are the two chiralities
proof:
(i) Existence for $W$: $w_{i}f = 0$ since $w_{i}$ anticommutes with the other $w_{j}$ and $w_{i}^{2} = 0$. Uniqueness: on the grade-$k$ state $v_{i_{1}}\cdots v_{i_{k}}f$, $w_{j}$ acts as zero if $j \notin \{i_{1}, \ldots, i_{k}\}$ and otherwise, using $w_{j}v_{i} = \delta_{ij} - v_{i}w_{j}$ (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}), removes the factor $v_{j}$ up to sign; so the common kernel of $w_{1}, \ldots, w_{m}$ on $S$ is the grade-zero line $\C f$. For $W'$ the same computation with the roles exchanged gives the top state, which every $v_{i}$ annihilates since $v_{i}^{2} = 0$. For a general $U$, Witt's theorem (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-extension}; as in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}) supplies an isometry $\rho$ with $\rho(W) = U$, and $\rho$ is the twisted adjoint action of a versor $R$ (Lemma \claimref{primer.twisted-adjoint-action}), $\rho(x) = \pm RxR^{-1}$; then $U(Rf) = \pm R(Wf)R^{-1}R = 0$, so $Rf$ is a pure spinor of $U$, and it is the only one up to scale because $R$ is invertible on $S$. Chirality: $I$ commutes with every even element, so $I$ acts on each grade as a scalar; explicitly
\[
I \;\propto\; \prod_{i}(v_{i}w_{i} - w_{i}v_{i}) \;=\; \prod_{i}(2v_{i}w_{i} - 1),
\]
and the $i$-th factor is $-1$ on states without $v_{i}$ and $+1$ on states with it, so the grade-$k$ states have chirality $\epsilon(-1)^{m-k}$ with $\epsilon$ the normalisation; every pure spinor, being a versor image of $f$, is a chirality eigenstate by (ii).

(ii) In even dimension $e_{j}I = -Ie_{j}$ for every basis vector (\claimref{std-algebra.pseudoscalar-commutation}), so $I$ commutes with even versors and anticommutes with odd ones; if $I\psi = \chi\psi$ then $I(R\psi) = \pm R I\psi = \pm\chi(R\psi)$ with the sign that of $R$'s parity.

(iii) Both chiralities occur among pure spinors (reflect $W$ in any non-null vector), chirality is constant on each orbit of the connected group by (ii), and the full isometry group, which is the connected group together with one reflection, is transitive by Witt; so there are exactly two orbits, one per chirality. For the Witt pair, $f$ has grade $0$ and the top state grade $m$, so their chiralities are $\epsilon(-1)^{m}$ and $\epsilon$: opposite exactly when $m$ is odd. Odd dimension: $-1$ is an improper isometry ($\det(-1) = (-1)^{2m+1}$) that fixes every subspace, so every orbit of the full group is an orbit of the connected group, and Witt's transitivity gives one family; and on either half $S_{\pm}$ the extra generator $\ell$ acts as the Fock grade parity up to a scalar (script-checked in dimensions five and seven), while the spin-algebra bivector $e_{1}\ell$ anticommutes with $\ell$, so the spin algebra mixes the Fock grades within each irreducible module.

The script builds $I$, $f$ and the top state on the split real forms of dimensions four, six and eight in \texttt{GA.py} and checks that both are eigenstates of $I$ with eigenvalues in the ratio $(-1)^{m}$ exactly (only the ratio is invariant, the sign of $I$ being a convention; the chiralities agree at $m = 2, 4$ and differ at $m = 3$), that $I$ anticommutes with every generator in even dimension and commutes with every generator in dimensions five and seven, and exhibits the exchanging versors with their parities. The classical result, with the general criterion that two maximal isotropic subspaces lie in one family exactly when their intersection has dimension congruent to $m$ modulo two, is Chevalley's \cite[Ch.~III, \S1]{Chevalley1954}, see also \cite{LawsonMichelsohn1989}; only the Witt-pair case is used here, and it is proved here.

title: The flag bit exists exactly at tower dimension $0 \bmod 4$
text: Let a tower have dimension $n$ and conformal completion with ambient $V$ of dimension $n + 2$, and let $W, W' \subset V_{\C}$ be a Witt pair, the two halves of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag} taken coherently across the pairs, with pure spinors the null blade $f$ and the top state (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.null-blades-fock-ideal-chirality}). Then the choice between $W$ and $W'$ is a discrete invariant of the connected conformal spin group, a \emph{bit}, if and only if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ (ambient dimension $2m$ with $m$ odd), and the bit is the chirality of the pure spinor, that is, the parity of the Fock grade of the complementary half's pure spinor ($0$ for $f$, $m$ for the top state). (i) The odd residues are odd-dimensional for every signature in the class, so the ambient is odd-dimensional, the pseudoscalar central, an even versor carries $W$ to $W'$, and the spin algebra mixes the Fock grades: no bit, on any window. (ii) The even residues carry the bit exactly at tower dimension $0 \bmod 4$: under Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} all four are at dimension four and carry it; the causal representatives of the alternative windows of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(iii), $(1,1)$ of $r = 0$ and $(1,5)$ of $r = 4$, do not. So the towers that can be oriented are the even residues $\{0, 2, 4, 6\}$ given P3, and the odd residues cannot be, given nothing.
proof:
By Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}(iii) the Witt pair lies in opposite families exactly when $\dim V_{\C} = 2m$ with $m$ odd, and a choice between $W$ and $W'$ that the connected group cannot undo is exactly a difference of family, since the connected group is transitive within a family (Witt together with Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}(ii)): so the bit exists if and only if $m$ is odd, and it is the chirality $\epsilon(-1)^{m}$ against $\epsilon$ of the two pure spinors, the Fock-grade parity of the top state $v_{1}\cdots v_{m}f$. With $2m = n + 2$, $m$ is odd if and only if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$. For this tower and the mirror (at dimension four, by \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives}), $\dim V_{\C} = 6$, $m = 3$: opposite families, the choice a bit; in ambient dimensions four and eight ($m = 2, 4$: $(1,1)$ and $(1,5)$) the top state has even grade, the same chirality as $f$, and there is no bit.

For odd $n$, $\dim V_{\C}$ is odd and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-families-are-two-chiralities}'s odd case applies: one family, the exchanging even versor exhibited in dimensions five and seven. The script corroborates with the exchanging isometry's determinant, $(-1)^{m}$ in even dimension and $+1$ in odd.

The listing choice of \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12} is the choice of which half of each pair annihilates, $f$ against the top state (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.null-blades-fock-ideal-chirality}). That odd residues are odd-dimensional only is $p - q \equiv p + q \pmod 2$, script-checked to dimension ten; a split real form suffices because every statement concerns $V_{\C}$, $S$ and $I$, shared by all real forms with the same complexification.

title: Which towers can carry the arrow
text:
The descent's orientation, and with it the asymmetry the flag sets in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, is undefined in the odd residues: $1, 3, 5, 7$ cannot be oriented and carry no asymmetry, whatever their content or window. It is defined in the even residues at their P3 representatives, all four-dimensional. Of those, $6$ and $2$ have one time, $4$ has none, and $0$ has two; so the towers that are both oriented and causal are this one and the mirror.

The two-time fork therefore leads to an \emph{oriented} tower: $(2,2)$ has ambient $\R^{3,3}$, $\mathrm{Spin}(3,3) \cong SL(4,\R)$, real four-component conformal spinors (real twistors: a minimal left ideal of $\Cl^+(3,3)$, whose pseudoscalar squares to $+1$, so there is no complex unit), three pairs, mass beginning at two by
\[
\det(\pi^{1}\tilde\pi^{1T} + \pi^{2}\tilde\pi^{2T}) \;=\; \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}\br{\tilde\pi^{1}\tilde\pi^{2}}, \qquad \br{\pi\rho} = \pi_{1}\rho_{2} - \pi_{2}\rho_{1},
\]
for the two real spinor parts of $\mathrm{Spin}(2,2) \cong SL(2,\R) \times SL(2,\R)$, and the Standard-Model gauge algebra by that paper's Proposition 4.3 in dimension four \cite[Prop.~4.3]{ButlerT12}, whose two conditionalities (mass-begins-at-two in dimension $n \neq 4$ as a hypothesis, and the identification of the gauge algebra with the automorphisms of minimal massive compositeness) it carries: a Kleinian copy of the Standard Model. Its share would be one only on two equalities the paper cannot supply off this tower's reversal orbit: the asymmetry per mode (P4, a premise on the fork) and the ceiling coupling (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}(c)). title: The fork's cost restated: the causal criterion is a theorem, and the bit on the fork is read once

title: Dark, stable, counted
Superselected, hence dark and exactly stable
text:
By Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} and the acoustic programme (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupling}, the series' acoustic no-go, at its mixed level: within the s-wave current algebra, with the sphere step conditional on the Indifference premise and the thermal state on premise (Q)), matter in a neighbouring tower gravitates on this metric and does nothing else observable at first order: dark by structural necessity, at that level. Stability is then not suppressed but exact, in three steps, the first of which is proved given the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The tower charge $r$ is superselected in the frozen phase: frozen-phase operators are built from the one soldering and preserve its signature (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), so portal matrix elements between residues vanish identically away from walls.
\item The walls are unreachable: singular loci ascend within-tower, since the completion adjoins exactly $(1,1)$ and preserves the residue (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), while the mod-8 shadow walls that separate residues are displaced successively away from the physical region, by the wall-sequence theorem of the sheaf paper \cite[\S5]{ButlerT4}, under that theorem's hypotheses (a compact base and good couplings at every stage), carried here.
\item Therefore the only inter-tower event in the universe's history is the descent itself: the towers communicated once, at the origin, and have been in absolute mutual darkness but for weight ever since. The singular locus of a black hole is an inter-tower event for energy, as it already was for weight, and never for the residue of any quantum: energy crosses at the wall, the residue does not (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}).
\end{enumerate}
One residue is flagged at observation level: dark-tower matter crossing this tower's horizons carries superselected charge the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold, which routes it into the tower-wise run of the singularity paper's ascend-then-descend structure \cite{ButlerT5}; the computation of that routing, with the mass range of its Gauss-law clause, is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.
proof: (1) Under the sector decomposition of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators} every frozen-phase local operator is a section of one tower's soldered bundle and acts within that tower's sector, so its matrix elements between distinct residues vanish: the tower charge is superselected, exactly. The hypothesis cannot be weakened to an algebraic one: an operator straddling two sectors would need a fibrewise map between $(A_{r}, V_{r})$ and $(A_{r'}, V_{r'})$ respecting both solderings, and although such maps exist abstractly (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}(ii)) none carries $V_{r}$ to $V_{r'}$. The shared metric is not a counterexample: gravity couples through stress-energy, which is built from the soldering and is residue-diagonal. (2) is the two imported theorems at their proved levels, the ascent's residue-invariance (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}) and the sheaf paper's conservation of degeneracy (\claimref{sheaf.infinite-wall-sequence}). (3) is the conjunction: no operator, no reachable wall, hence no channel; the descent, which built all the towers at once, is the one shared event. This is the series' one-way-door argument run tower-wise, with soldered locality in place of locality. The opening clause, darkness, is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-gravity-only-coupling} under P1 (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}).

title: The mirror tower is a copy of this one
proof:
The list of inputs is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain}, whose own lemmas (pair count, Segre) are statements about $V_{\C}$ and about tensor products of complex spaces. Invariance item by item.

Complexification: $\R^{2,4} \otimes \C = \R^{4,2} \otimes \C$ as quadratic spaces, there being no signature over $\C$. Even subalgebra: $e_{i} \mapsto e_{i}e_{n}$ ($i < n$) identifies $\Cl^{0}(p,q)$ with $\Cl(p, q-1)$ when $e_{n}^{2} = -1$; the script verifies the relations exactly for $(2,4)$ and $(4,2)$, and Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}'s computation gives $\Cl(2,3)$ and $\Cl(4,1)$ the same type, centre and module dimension, both $\Mat(4,\C)$. The spin group (even versors with $R\tilde{R} = 1$) and the invariant form $\bar{\psi}\varphi$ on $\Cl^{0}f$ are defined by the even subalgebra and the ambient reversion, which the reversal leaves unchanged, since $(p,q) \mapsto (q,p)$ changes the signs of vector squares and not the order of products. Under $e_{i} \mapsto e_{i}e_{n}$ the ambient reversion becomes Clifford conjugation of $\Cl(2,3)$, the antilinear involution a hermitian form needs, and the form so built has signature $(2,2)$: the spin group is $SU(2,2)$ in both cases, with the same representation on the conformal spinor space $\CS$, the minimal left ideal of the even algebra (likewise $\Cl^{0}(1,3) \cong \Cl(1,2)$ and $\Cl^{0}(3,1) \cong \Cl(3,0)$ are both $\Mat(2,\C)$, with the same Lorentz spin group and Weyl spinors).

\[
(\star F)_{ab} \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{|g|}\,\epsilon_{abcd}\,g^{ce}g^{df}F_{ef},
\]
even in $g$, so $F \wedge \star F$ and $F \wedge F$ are reversal-invariant.

(i) follows by running the paper's chain on the reversed data; (ii) is the observation that the real module of $\Cl(p,q)$ appears nowhere in the list. \[
f_{2} \;=\; \frac{\epsilon_{2}}{\epsilon}\cdot\frac{n_{2}}{n_{6}}\cdot\frac{m_{2}}{m_{6}} \;=\; 1 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 .
\] (iv) is the audit clause of Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} read in the direction it permits.

title: The stored asymmetry is a charge, not a number
text:
Under the classification of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}, with $\epsilon$ initial data of the descent, inherited rather than generated, and the number $N$ common to the towers under P1 ($N = M_{P}/H$, which fixes the boundary mode count, about $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, without being it: Observation \claimref{standard-model.largeness-number-universes-boundary-modes}; the argument uses only that $N$ is common):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge.)} The asymmetry stored in an oriented tower is the charge $Q = \epsilon N$, fixed by the descent's data and independent of the tower's temperature; it is not a thermal number $n - \bar{n} \propto g\,\mu T^{2}$. So the mirror share $f_{2} = 1$ holds at any mirror temperature: a cold mirror carries the same baryon charge as this tower in the same number of baryons, with negligible mirror radiation.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Origin.)} The charge is the descent's and cannot be produced afterwards: the one channel superselection leaves open, gravitational production from the visible plasma (the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows''), yields $1.8$ to $2.7 \times 10^{-15}$ mirror quanta per unit entropy at the ceiling reheating against the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy that our baryon number requires, more than four orders too few even counting every produced quantum as a baryon. Black holes are a sink for $Q$, not a source (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(iv), under P5): a mass-preserving rearrangement that erodes each tower's free baryon count and moves no share.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Temperature.)} Taken as a free datum of the descent, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$, which the record excludes), the mirror's temperature ratio $\xi = T'/T$ is bounded below by the gravitational floor, $\xi$ between $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii), the bracket the species-counting ambiguity; four parts in a thousand of this at the bottom of the ceiling range), and above by the $\Neff$ cap at $0.448$; a deposit of each unit of baryon number with energy of order the reheating temperature puts it at $\xi \approx 4 \times 10^{-3}$. The paper carries the whole interval. With $\eta = n_{B}/n_{\gamma} = 6.1 \times 10^{-10}$ here and equal baryon number,
\[
\eta' \;=\; \frac{\eta}{\xi^{3}}
\]
runs from $19$ to $26$ at the floor down to about $0.008$ at the hot deposit, crossing one at $\xi = \eta^{1/3} = 8.5 \times 10^{-4}$: at least $10^{7}$ times ours throughout, with $\Delta\Neff$ eight orders or more below the cap.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The two readings.)} The thermal reading would give $f_{2} \sim \xi_{2}^{3}$ instead, at most $0.090$ under the $\Neff$ cap ($0.448^{3}$) and $10^{-7}$ or less anywhere in the interval; the two readings cannot both hold, and the paper's own classification decides for the charge.
\end{enumerate}
Level: the classification is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-trichotomy-descents-data}'s; the incompatibility is arithmetic. The mirror's nucleosynthesis, which is not a copy of ours and on which the burning branch of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i) and the composition caveat of refutation item 6 rest, follows the proof, at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the proof's thermal up-down ratio at freeze-out fails at the floor, where the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons; it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$, an interval containing the hot-deposit estimate (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}). The burning branch is therefore not the floor's composition.

title: Dark, stable, counted
text:
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Discussion of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}: the interval, and the mirror's nucleosynthesis.} The paper's own mechanism favours the hot end (the tower charges are created at the freezing in quanta of order the reheating temperature), but the nucleosynthesis is computed at the floor, the one value the framework fixes, the hot end being the trivial case; the interval straddles the crossover of $\eta'$ at one, charge-dominated below it, and statements that hold only at the charge-dominated end are labelled ``at the floor''.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{Weak freeze-out and the burning branch.} The mirror's expansion rate is set by the visible plasma at $T = T'/\xi$, so its weak rate over the Hubble rate scales as $T'^{3}$: at the floor it crosses one at $T' \approx 0.43$ to $0.45$ GeV, above the mirror's QCD crossover at $155$ MeV At the floor the mirror's weak interactions froze out with its quarks free and the up-down ratio thermal (at the hot end the crossing falls below $100$ MeV, under the crossover but still where $n/p \approx 1$), so the neutron-to-proton ratio at hadronisation is near one and burning is the framework's expectation. A proton-only mirror would need a mirror lepton asymmetry large enough to bias that ratio, a datum the framework does not fix; it is carried as the alternative branch.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{The bottleneck and the reheat, at the floor.} The deuterium bottleneck opens near $T' = 0.23$ to $0.24$ MeV, not at our $0.062$, at a baryon density of $0.8$ to $1.2 \times 10^{31}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and a cosmic time of microseconds, so mirror neutrons cannot decay first and whatever can burn, burns (by then $T'/T$ has risen by about $2.6$ from its seeded value through the two sectors' separate entropy conservation, leaving $\eta'$ within ten percent). The released $7.07$ MeV per nucleon enters a plasma carrying $25$ to $33$ keV of photon energy per baryon and $2.75$ times that with pairs (thermal pairs at zero chemical potential, a lower bound on the budget, so the reheating factor below is an upper bound), so complete burning would reheat the mirror by $3.0$ to $3.2$, to $T' \approx 0.70$ to $0.78$ MeV and $\eta' \approx 0.72$ to $0.81$. Photodisintegration makes the endpoint a nuclear-statistical-equilibrium problem that completes only as expansion cools it; the figures are the completion limit. At the hot end burning does not reheat the mirror appreciably.

\smallskip\noindent\emph{Recombination, and the caveat on imported bounds.} On the burning branch the mirror is helium. It recombines earlier than we do because its photons are fewer, at $T'$ between about $0.55$ eV at the hot end and $0.68$ eV at the floor after its burning ($0.85$ eV on the proton-only branch, and higher still for helium), at a visible temperature between $0.1$ and $0.8$ keV across the interval. So bounds derived for a mirror sector with our $\eta$ assume a baryon-to-photon ratio, and on the burning branch a composition, nothing like the mirror's; the mirror-galaxy analysis of refutation item 6 rescales $\eta'$ and includes a helium mirror, but only at the hot end of the interval.

title: The mirror share is one, and how fragile that is
text:
Write $m_{r} = c_{r}\Lambda_{r}$, with $\Lambda_{r}$ the confinement scale of tower $r$'s non-abelian sector and $c_{r}$ the constituent factor of its lightest charge-carrying composite.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The mirror.)} By Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$ exactly, hence $f_{2} = 1$ under P4, which Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v) discharges for the mirror, an isomorphism of theories rather than a one-loop statement. As a ratio of mass densities it is a ratio of mean mass per baryon: ours is about $936.7$ MeV after helium, a mirror burnt entirely to helium (the completion limit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}'s burning branch) gives $931.8$ MeV, so $f_{2}$ is $0.995$ in that limit and $1$ on the proton-only branch, a one-sided systematic of half a percent at assembly level. Caveat (T14c): the two branches bracket the share where the mirror is helium or protons; at the gravitational floor the mirror is degenerate and, for a copied lepton number $L \leq 0$, ends $96$ to $100$ percent neutrons, a composition neither branch describes, and it is helium only for $\xi$ between about $3 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2 \times 10^{-2}$ (Computation \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-composition}); the half-percent bracket is established there and not at the floor.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Fragility.)} The equality is unstable to any departure from the copy. Suppose the two towers shared a ceiling $M$ and coupling but differed in light content by $\Delta b$ over the running range, with $b_{6} \leq 11$; then at one loop
\[
\ln\frac{\Lambda_{2}}{\Lambda_{6}} \;\geq\; \frac{\Delta b}{b_{6} + \Delta b}\,\ln\frac{M}{\Lambda_{6}}.
\]
One Dirac flavour is $\Delta b = 2/3$, which with $\Lambda_{6} = 0.3$ GeV moves the mirror share by a factor between $4.89$ (bottom of the ceiling range, $b_{6} = 11$) and $21.4$ (top, $b_{6} = 7$), past the observed $5.364$ everywhere except at the bottom of the range on the most conservative branch. A coupling departure $\delta = \alpha_{2}(M)^{-1} - \alpha_{6}(M)^{-1}$ at the ceiling with identical content moves $\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6}$ by $e^{-2\pi\delta/b}$, a factor $2.45$ per unit at $b = 7$, so the share stays within ten percent of one only for $|\delta| < 0.106$. So $f_{2} = 1$ is exact, P2-protected, and fragile.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The odd towers.)} In three and five dimensions the gauge coupling is dimensionful and the confinement scale is set by the coupling itself ($\Lambda_{3} \sim g_{3}^{2}N$, $\Lambda_{5} \sim 1/g_{5}^{2}$), so nothing about $\Lambda_{1,7,3,5}$ follows without a rule the series does not derive (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}); the unit-ball rule of the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule'' constrains that rule, as shares per unit of our volume, without supplying it.
\end{enumerate}
Level: (i) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}; (ii) is one-loop arithmetic under its stated assumptions, flagged; (iii) is a scope statement.
proof:
(i) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iii), with Premise P4 discharged for the mirror by that theorem's clause (v). (ii): one loop,
\[
\alpha(\mu)^{-1} \;=\; \alpha(M)^{-1} - \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{\mu}^{M} b\,d\ln\mu'
\]
for an asymptotically free sector, with $\Lambda$ the scale at which $\alpha^{-1}$ vanishes. With equal $\alpha(M)^{-1}$ and $b_{2} - b_{6} \geq \Delta b$,
\[
\alpha_{2}(\mu)^{-1} \;\leq\; \alpha_{6}(\mu)^{-1} - \frac{\Delta b}{2\pi}\ln\frac{M}{\mu};
\]
at $\mu = \Lambda_{2}$ the left side vanishes, so
\[
\frac{\Delta b}{2\pi}\ln\frac{M}{\Lambda_{2}} \;\leq\; \alpha_{6}(\Lambda_{2})^{-1} \;\leq\; \frac{b_{6}^{\max}}{2\pi}\ln\frac{\Lambda_{2}}{\Lambda_{6}}.
\]
Writing $L = \ln(\Lambda_{2}/\Lambda_{6})$ and $L_{0} = \ln(M/\Lambda_{6})$,
\[
b_{6}^{\max}L \;\geq\; \Delta b\,(L_{0} - L), \qquad\text{so}\qquad L \;\geq\; \frac{\Delta b\,L_{0}}{b_{6}^{\max} + \Delta b};
\]
the script checks the chain as exact rational algebra and evaluates the factors at both ends of the ceiling range, the two readings of Hypothesis (U) in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} ($L_{0} = 35.23$ and $27.79$; $7.49$, $21.4$ at the top and $4.89$, $11.2$ at the bottom for $\Delta b = 2/3$; $18.84$ for $\Delta b = 1$). The coupling sensitivity is $\Lambda = M e^{-2\pi/(b\alpha(M))}$ differentiated, $d\ln\Lambda/d(\alpha^{-1}) = -2\pi/b$. (iii) is dimensional analysis: $[g^{2}] = \text{mass}^{4-d}$, with the absence of a coupling rule from Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}.

title: The mirror share, assembled
text:
Under Premises \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} and \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p4-democracy-asymmetry-over-oriented-towers} being discharged for the mirror, clause (iii)), the Standard-Model paper's Hypothesis (S) as carried in Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}, and the input list of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain}, the mirror tower contributes exactly one visible share:
\[
f_{2} \;=\; \underbrace{\frac{\epsilon_{2}}{\epsilon_{6}}}_{\text{P2}}\cdot\;\underbrace{\frac{n_{2}}{n_{6}}}_{\text{derived}}\;\cdot\;\underbrace{\frac{m_{2}}{m_{6}}}_{\text{derived, given P2}} \;=\; 1\cdot 1\cdot 1 \;=\; 1, \qquad \Omega_{\mathrm{mirror}} \;=\; \Omega_{b},
\]
exactly on the proton-only branch and to half a percent on the burning branch (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i)). The three factors are stated separately because they have three standings, and the exposure of the share is the weakest of them.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The mode ratio: derived, on no premise of this paper.)} $n_{2} = n_{6}$, the same state space.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The mass ratio: derived, given P2.)} $m_{2} = m_{6}$ up to the two sectors' composition, the common ceiling coupling being P2 along the reversal orbit.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The asymmetry ratio: premised on P2.)} $\epsilon_{2} = \epsilon_{6}$ by the audit along the same orbit (P1's orientation clause a weaker second route); P4 is discharged for the mirror, not assumed.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(No temperature in it.)} The share is one anywhere in the interval of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(iii).
\end{enumerate}
proof:
The product is the tower factor of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent} evaluated at $r = 2$. (i) Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain} lists the data the Standard-Model chain consumes and Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one} shows each invariant under the reversal, so the mirror's derived content is this tower's, the ground type never entering (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(i), (ii)), and $n_{2}/n_{6} = 1$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mode-counts-two-modules-which-one}(iv)); this uses Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain} and Hypothesis (S) (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) as carried in Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}, and no premise of this paper. (ii) Identical content gives identical $\beta$-functions in any scheme and to all orders, so the common ceiling coupling, Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} along the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv)), gives $\Lambda_{2} = \Lambda_{6}$ and $c_{2} = c_{6}$; what remains of $m_{2}/m_{6}$ is the ratio of mean mass per baryon, $0.995$ in the helium completion limit and $1$ on the proton-only branch (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(i)). (iii) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v), first route, which discharges \claimref{dark-matter.p4-democracy-asymmetry-over-oriented-towers} for the mirror. (iv) $Q = \epsilon N$ is a charge of the descent, $N$ common under P1 (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}), and no factor depends on $\xi$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(i)); the thermal reading is excluded by that classification, not by this proof (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}(iv)). With the dilution of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}, common to the towers, $\Omega_{\mathrm{mirror}} = f_{2}\,\Omega_{b} = \Omega_{b}$.

Level: (i) proved given Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain} and Hypothesis (S); (ii) proved given (i) and Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}, the half percent at assembly level; (iii) premised on Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}; (iv) proved given the classification of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}. title: What the share is exposed to, and what it is not
text: Every factor of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-assembled} is a ratio between two towers, so the share is one whatever content $X$ the Standard-Model chain produces from Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain}, correct or not: the reversal carries $X$ to $X$.
