title: Which towers are populated
text: The census says which towers can hold matter; it does not say which the descent filled, and the two are at different levels. This tower is populated by observation. The mirror is populated by P2: residues $6$ and $2$ are equivalent under signature reversal, so a descent that filled one filled the other, at the same asymmetry (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)); this is the one case in which population is derived. The four odd towers are reached by nothing in the series: P2 does not equate them with this tower, the tower paper gives them algebras and not contents, and what the descent deposited in each is the pre-descent theory's, successor problem (2). What supports their population is the record read inside the framework: with the mirror's share exactly one, an empty set of odd towers would make the ratio $1$ against the observed $5.364$, and the framework has no other dark candidate, so, granted the framework, the observed remainder is the evidence that the odd towers hold matter. That is an inference at observation level, not a count, and it is what the unit-ball rule presupposes when it sums over six towers (Premise \claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}). Nothing derived in this paper depends on the odd towers being populated: the mirror share, the superselection, the parity theorem and the arrow are the same if they are empty, and refutation item 6 says so.

title: The arrow counted
The asymmetry: the arrow counted, and the fifteenth refutation
text:
The framework does not generate its asymmetry; it inherits it.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Sakharov.)} The Sakharov conditions are for generating an asymmetry dynamically from a symmetric state; a universe whose asymmetry is initial data does not need them. The descent supplies the reason the initial data need not be symmetric: it is irreversible (the lossy projection of the taxonomy paper's descent theorem \cite{ButlerT1}), it creates the tower charges, and it makes one orientation choice, the Witt flag, which is what particle-versus-antiparticle means (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}). Each matches a Sakharov condition in name; none is a mechanism producing a number.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The fifteenth refutation.)} A pre-descent $\theta$-term would source asymmetry through the topology of gauge bundles; but it integrates a characteristic class, of even degree, so the odd-dimensional towers carry no continuous $\theta$, and at the P3 representatives a $\theta$-term exists exactly where a flag bit does. In this tower it is excluded empirically: a $\theta$-routed asymmetry needs an angle of order one at the descent that does not relax before it acts, and the neutron dipole bound $|d_{n}| < 1.8 \times 10^{-26}\,e\,$cm \cite{Abel2020} gives $|\theta| \lesssim 10^{-10}$ today (through a hadronic matrix element with its own uncertainty). Not excluded, and not claimed: an angle that relaxes or rolls; and the mirror's angle, which equals ours only by P2 along the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv)), the copy being of the functional, not its coefficient. Internally the paper says only that the orientation is the one mechanism the framework itself supplies; that locates the mechanism and does not refute the alternative.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Confinement and universality.)} The orientation route is one bit spent once (uniqueness among all conceivable mechanisms is not claimed). A flag exists on every rung of every tower (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}), but the flag \emph{bit} only in the even residues at their P3 representatives (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}), so the asymmetry is confined to the oriented causal towers, this one and the mirror, and the odd towers carry none by either route. Universality of the value is Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p4-democracy-asymmetry-over-oriented-towers}, a theorem for the mirror (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)) and not extendable to inequivalent towers, the asymmetry per mode depending on the tower's own charge structure.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The value, a stance.)} $\epsilon$ is not derived here and not classified. The trichotomy's kinematic clause runs for it as for $N$ ($\epsilon$ is continuous), at that Fact's observation level; the dynamical clause does not, since generating an asymmetry from CPT-invariant dynamics is exactly what the Sakharov mechanism does. \emph{Stance, flagged and attacked in the section ``The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper'':} the framework inherits its asymmetry, and $\epsilon$ is initial data of the descent, refuted by any in-framework calculation that produces $\epsilon$ dynamically. The count uses only the equality of $\epsilon$ across the reversal orbit (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v)), not its provenance. On the stance the unexplained numbers are two, $N$ and $\epsilon$, with the orientation bit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation} a third datum of the same event.
\end{enumerate}
proof: The refutation in (ii) is a degree count. A $\theta$-term integrates over the tower's space a characteristic class of the gauge bundle ($\tr F \wedge F$ in four dimensions); Chern and Pontryagin classes have even degree, so in odd dimension there is no top-degree class and no continuous $\theta$. Homotopy agrees: bundles on $S^{d}$ are classified by $\pi_{d-1}(G)$, zero in three dimensions ($\pi_{2}(G) = 0$), and in five $\pi_{4}(SU(2)) = \mathbb{Z}_{2}$ allows only a discrete angle, $0$ or $\pi$, with $\pi_{4}(SU(n)) = 0$ for $n \geq 3$; the odd-dimensional Chern-Simons term is a quantised level, not an angle. (iii) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension} with Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p4-democracy-asymmetry-over-oriented-towers} and Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v); (iv) is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-trichotomy-descents-data}(1) at its level, $\epsilon$ being continuous. The degree computation is recorded in the script. Clause (i) rests on Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}, which supplies the one-handed listing choice that is the particle-antiparticle orientation, read here as the descent's flag.

title: The orientation is the arrow: the seventeenth refutation
text:
The Standard-Model paper left one absolute bit undetermined, the particle-antiparticle orientation, expected to be fixed by the charge-zero condition. The expectation is refuted by a $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ covariance argument parallel to the trichotomy's rescaling one, on three premises: that CPT conjugation $C$ is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure and leaves every action functional $S_{\mu}$ of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} invariant, $S_{\mu}\circ C = S_{\mu}$, the gauge couplings included (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}; checked in the proof for the metric, the completion, the pairing and the action; premised for the imported gauge sector and for structures later papers add); Hypothesis (S), under which the Standard-Model paper's chirality proposition, the source of the relative-versus-absolute split, is proved (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}); and that the orientation flag is a datum of each solution, the sign of its complex structure relative to the Fock module's unit planted by the descent and not part of the kinematic structure (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}; were it kinematic, the bit would be constant on every solution space, hence dynamically fixed within each of two isomorphic theories, and the conclusion below would fail). Here $C$ is the composite of grade involution, reversal and the flag conjugate, an anti-automorphism; acting on fields as a symmetry does (vectors by its vector part, connections through the induced Lie algebra automorphism), it is $\mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, with $\kappa$ complex conjugation, so it is antilinear (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}).

Anything the structures determine is conjugation-invariant, and the orientation is not. The charge-zero condition fixes all \emph{relative} structure \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12}; under that reading the absolute bit is not kinematic, and since conjugation maps each solution space onto itself and exchanges the two orientations, the bit takes both values on every nonempty solution space: it is initial data in the sense of clause (I) of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape}, and so neither dynamically fixed nor a parameter of the laws (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are}). No exhaustiveness of the kinematic, dynamical and initial-data alternatives is used. It is the Witt flag of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}: the open orientation of the content derivation and the arrow of time are one choice, made once.

The descent measure carries two numbers and one bit. The neutrino sector supplies no orientation refutation condition: the identification of $\nu_{R}$ with the hypercharge-zero singlet at grade zero is flag-covariant (the conjugate flag exchanges the singlet grades zero and three), so no completion of the orientation could exclude it \cite{ButlerT15}.

This is the seventeenth refutation (the sixteenth is the neutrino paper's \cite[Prop.~4.1(1)]{ButlerT15}), in the pattern of the thirteenth and the trichotomy: what the framework cannot determine, it can prove it cannot determine, and locate.
proof:
CPT conjugation is the composition of grade involution, reversal, and the flag conjugate $v_{k} \leftrightarrow w_{k}$ (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) on each tower's Clifford bundle; the grade involution negates every vector, the timelike one included (the T; the spatial inversion is the P). Because of the reversal the composite is an anti-automorphism, and it acts on fields as a symmetry does (the convention stated in \claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}): on vectors by its vector part, and on a connection through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, so that curvature is fixed. In that convention it acts on fields as $C = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$, $\kappa$ complex conjugation: its vector part $-1$ is the rotor $I_{6}$, and the flag conjugate that preserves the frozen point's action is complex conjugation, which carries the flag $W$ to $\overline W$, in the other family (\claimref{synthesis.cpt-conjugation-pseudoscalar-rotor-times-complex-conjugation}). So $C$ is antilinear. Structure by structure: the fibre metric is fixed by grade involution, reversal and the exchange of a null pair, which is an isometry of the completion's hyperbolic plane; the pairing on the Fock module sends the grade-$k$ state to the grade-$(3-k)$ state \cite[Prop.~5.6]{ButlerT12} (\claimref{standard-model.chirality-two-halves-spinor-module-conjugation}), which is exactly what the flag conjugate does; and the action is the frozen point's, built from the metric and the completion. The derived gauge sector (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-inputs-standard-model-chain}) is CPT-even by the standard theorem for local Lorentz-invariant actions, but that theorem concerns the antiunitary CPT operator of quantum field theory; that $C$, antilinear and so of Wigner's antiunitary type, realises that operator is argued, not proved, so the gauge sector's CPT-evenness is imported and carried as a premise (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-cpt-covariance}).

So $C$ is an isomorphism of the kinematic data exchanging the flag's two orientations, and a quantity the structures determine would be fixed by it while the orientation is not. The last step reads the bit against Definition \claimref{obj.dark-energy.four-ways-number-enters-theory-shape} directly. Let $S_{\mu}$ be the action functionals, $\mu$ the norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ of the frozen point together with whatever couplings the imported gauge sector carries, and $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$ their solution spaces. The premise's clause for the action says $S_{\mu} \circ C = S_{\mu}$ for every $\mu$, the gauge couplings included; for the norm this is visible directly, since $C$ sends the real vector $I$ to $-I$, so $Q(CI) = Q(I)$ and $C$ does not move $\mu$, and for the gauge couplings it is the premise. A critical point of a $C$-invariant functional is carried by the involution $C$ to a critical point of the same functional, so $C(\mathcal{S}_{\mu}) = \mathcal{S}_{\mu}$ for every $\mu$. Let $q = \pm 1$ be the orientation bit, a function of the solution (the descent plants its flag once, Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}, so $q$ is conserved). By the premise that the flag is a datum (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}), the sign of the flag's complex structure $J$ relative to the Fock module's $i$ is configuration data of each solution, planted by the descent on the three-pair structure, and not part of the kinematic structure: were it kinematic, the bit would be constant on every solution space of the theory carrying it, hence (D) there, and the two orientations would be two isomorphic theories rather than two solutions of one. Under that premise, $C$ exchanges the two orientations, $q(Cx) = -q(x)$. For every $\mu$ with $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$ nonempty, which holds for the $\mu$ of our universe, $q$ therefore takes both values on $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$, so it is not constant on $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$: $q$ is (I). By Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.four-alternatives-are-exhaustive-three-are} it is then neither (D) nor (P), each of which requires constancy on every $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$; and it is not (K), since $x$ and $Cx$ have isomorphic kinematic structures, $C$ being that isomorphism, while $q(Cx) \neq q(x)$. The step excludes a parameter of the laws for the bit directly, because a parameter of the laws is constant on each solution space and the bit is not; no exhaustiveness of the kinematic, dynamical and initial-data alternatives enters. The relative-versus-absolute split is the Standard-Model paper's chirality proposition, imported under Hypothesis (S) (\claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-derived-generation-flag}); the flag-covariance of the $\nu_{R}$ identification is the exchange of the singlet grades, which the legacy script verifies on the three-pair Fock model. The script of this version tests the logical step and the frozen-point part of the action, not the premises: it applies $C = \mathrm{Ad}(I_{6}) \circ \kappa$ explicitly, in Gaussian rational arithmetic, and confirms that on fixed rational data in the six-dimensional ambient space it is $-1$ on vectors, fixes the curvature bivector, and fixes the norms and the integrand $\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$, that on complexified data it is antilinear and carries each of them to its complex conjugate (with controls in which negating $I$ alone, or a real-linear flag conjugate in place of $\kappa$, flips the integrand), that the flag conjugate, on the split real form, is an isometry of the three null pairs exchanging the two pure vacua $v_{1}v_{2}v_{3}$ and $w_{1}w_{2}w_{3}$, and, exhaustively on small finite theories, that a $C$-odd quantity on $C$-stable solution spaces is (I) and not (K), with a control in which dropping $C$-stability makes it (P).

title: Point of contact: one datum for two questions
text: Matter over antimatter and the direction of time are one datum, the descent's orientation bit, spent once and read twice: unexplained, provably, and named beside $N$ and $\epsilon$ \cite{ButlerT17}.

title: The audits
The audits
text: The count and the radiation audit both depend on how a tower of dimension other than four gravitates on the one metric, and the two can be made to contradict each other by answering it differently in two places (a five-dimensional photon diluting as $a^{-5}$ per volume of its own space while five-dimensional matter is counted as $a^{-3}$ per shared volume). The sourcing rule is fixed first, as the reading of P1 it is, and both audits are run from it.

title: Projection: every tower's content dilutes as this one's
text: Read Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} as the sourcing rule: the one metric is the four-dimensional one, a tower shares its three spatial directions and its time, and the tower's contribution to the metric's source is its energy per unit of the shared three-volume, its content taken homogeneous along every direction it has. Then, for a tower of any dimension, with the extra directions (if any) either co-expanding with the shared scale factor $a$ or static, and with a missing shared direction (the three-dimensional towers, which contain two of the three shared spatial directions) filled by a family of sheets, comoving in the background and displaced with the matter in perturbations (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress}), one per unit of comoving length along the missing direction, the projected energy density of non-relativistic matter dilutes as $a^{-3}$ and that of radiation (the zero modes along any static extra direction) as $a^{-4}$, exactly as in this tower. No tower is diluted away or into prominence relative to this one.
proof:
Let the tower have $D$ spatial directions, $D - 3 = e \geq 0$ of them extra. Co-expanding case: number density per unit $D$-volume scales as $a^{-D}$, and a massless quantum's energy as $a^{-1}$, so the densities per $D$-volume are $a^{-D}$ (matter) and $a^{-(D+1)}$ (radiation); the extra directions have length proportional to $a$, so integrating over them multiplies by $a^{e}$, giving $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$. Static case: the extra directions have fixed length, number density per $D$-volume scales as $a^{-3}$, a massless quantum with no momentum along the static directions redshifts as $a^{-1}$, and integration over the fixed length changes no power: $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$ again (a quantum with momentum along a static direction keeps that momentum and behaves as a massive four-dimensional mode, hence as matter).

For $e < 0$, the three-dimensional towers, the missing shared direction is filled as the hypothesis states, by a comoving family of sheets: the density per unit two-volume within a sheet scales as $a^{-2}$ (matter) or $a^{-3}$ (radiation), and the number of sheets per unit proper length along the missing direction as $a^{-1}$, giving $a^{-3}$ and $a^{-4}$.

The other reading, a single sheet of fixed proper thickness, violates the homogeneity clause of the rule (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}, read as the sourcing rule) and would give $a^{-2}$ and $a^{-3}$, under which the three-dimensional towers would grow relative to everything else; it is named because two of the four odd towers are exactly these. The exponent arithmetic is script-checked as a function of the rule (expanding directions, static extra directions, sheet families) for $D = 2, 3, 4$.

title: The radiation audit: what the type-by-residue theorem closes, and what stays open
text:
The cosmic microwave background caps extra relativistic energy at $\Delta\Neff \lesssim 0.3$ \cite{Planck2018}, and one massless photon-like species (two polarisations) at the visible temperature contributes $\Delta\Neff = (8/7)(11/4)^{4/3} \approx 4.4$, so five democratically filled sectors with such photons would contribute of order twenty. The audit proceeds tower by tower, at two levels fixed by Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can} and Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries}: the \emph{ground} level, where the type decides whether the tower's spinors carry an intrinsic $U(1)$ (exactly at the complex member of each odd pair, $r = 3, 7$ in the paper's convention), and the \emph{rung} level, where every flagged tower carries abelian charges from its ladder pairs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The mirror tower, $r = 2$.)} Open, by theorem: the mirror's derived content is a copy of ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so it has a massless mirror photon and three light mirror neutrinos. The ground level is closed for the real member of the pair $\{2, 6\}$ (intrinsic group $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(i); which member depends on the labelling convention, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}) and irrelevant, since the content is not at that level. This is the mirror-matter situation of the literature, costed in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}.
\item \emph{(The three-dimensional towers, $r = 1, 7$.)} Closed at both levels: vector-like (no chirality in odd dimension), so Dirac masses are unforbidden and generic; with no massless charged matter left, each compact $U(1)$ in three dimensions, the intrinsic one of the complex member of $\{1, 7\}$ (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii)) and the rung-level ones of both, leaves no massless photon. The paper states that every such $U(1)$ confines by monopoles \cite{Polyakov1977}; with the half-integral bare Chern-Simons level that the parity anomaly forces (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.anomalies}(i)), that holds in the confining phase (C) only, and in phase (T) the photon is instead topologically massive (Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.three-dimensional-phases}); both phases close the channel. The non-abelian factors confine.
\item \emph{(The five-dimensional towers, $r = 3, 5$.)} Open at both levels: the complex member of the pair $\{3, 5\}$ carries an intrinsic $U(1)$ by theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii); which member depends on the convention), both carry rung-level ones, no Polyakov mechanism exists in five dimensions, and by Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} a surviving photon dilutes as $a^{-4}$, exactly as ours.
\item \emph{(The Goldstone exposure.)} Confining dark sectors with chiral breaking could leave massless dark pions. The framework supplies its own gap: any tower's accidental global symmetries are broken by its own tower's higher rungs (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so the Goldstones are pseudo-Goldstones with masses of order $\Lambda_{\mathrm{conf}}^{2}/M_{\mathrm{rung}}$, the existence input a theorem and the mass estimate dimensional analysis.
\end{enumerate}
Conclusion: the three-dimensional towers are closed by theorem plus Polyakov confinement or, in phase (T), topological mass; the mirror tower is open by theorem, with a known relativistic content, and closes only if it is cold, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} is an exception to P2 (applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), P2 gives $\xi = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$); the five-dimensional towers are open with a content this paper does not derive. By the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows'' (proved given the imported rate) every dark tower's temperature is bounded below by gravitational heating at a few parts in ten thousand of the visible temperature at the top of the ceiling range, and above by whatever energy the descent deposited, which the $\Neff$ cap limits to $0.448$ for the mirror and the paper's hot-deposit estimate puts near $4 \times 10^{-3}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}); across that interval both the mirror's channel and the five-dimensional towers' close by eight orders or more (twelve at the floor; the one case below eight is a nine-vector tower at the hot end, at $7.4$). $\Delta\Neff \approx 0$ is therefore a conditional stance, conditional on the open channels closing by one of the routes of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs} and on the deposit being no hotter than the estimate; so registered, and stated with that cost.

On self-interaction: in the three-dimensional towers it is at composite strength if their matter is the confined charged matter the closure leaves, which the series does not establish (the section ``The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy''); in the five-dimensional ones it is undetermined; and for the mirror the composite figure is the wrong one, since mirror matter recombines at a visible temperature of order a keV (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}) and enters structure formation as neutral mirror atoms, with an elastic cross-section per mass of order $2 \times 10^{8}$ (hydrogen) or $5 \times 10^{7}$ (helium) $\mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$, and as a plasma once ionised inside a halo: collisional and dissipative like our gas, tested by the collisional-fraction and dark-disk bounds of refutation item 6. The rung-breaking scale of channel (4) is valued in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success}.
proof: The $\Delta\Neff$ cost of a species: one neutrino species carries $(7/8)(4/11)^{4/3}$ of the photon energy density, so a two-polarisation boson at the photon temperature counts as $(8/7)(11/4)^{4/3} \approx 4.40$ neutrino species; the script brackets this exactly. (1) is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(i); the ground-level remark is Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(i). (2) Odd-dimensional towers admit no chirality, so mass terms are unforbidden; Polyakov's theorem is imported at its own level and applies to every compact $U(1)$ once the charged matter is massive, whatever the charge's origin. (3) Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(ii) for the intrinsic $U(1)$, Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries} for the rung ones, Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} for the $a^{-4}$; the absence of a Polyakov mechanism is the standard fact that monopole confinement of a compact $U(1)$ is specific to three dimensions. (4) is the effective-field-theory estimate, at the rung scale valued in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} under Hypothesis (U), with its existence input a theorem: the rung operators exist at every level (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}) and break any accidental symmetry not protected by the tower's own structure. The conclusion is the conjunction, with the dark temperatures bounded below by Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature} and above by the deposit estimate of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, and the closing routes those of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}.

title: The open channels, with their costs
text:
\emph{The mirror tower.} Its relativistic content is a copy of ours, so at recombination its radiation is $\rho'_{\mathrm{rad}} = (T'/T_{\gamma})^{4}\,\rho_{\mathrm{rad}}$ with $T'$ the mirror photon temperature and the same internal thermal history; in neutrino units the visible radiation is
\[
\Neff^{\mathrm{tot}} \;=\; \frac{8}{7}\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)^{4/3} + 3.044 \;=\; 7.447, \qquad\text{so}\qquad \Delta\Neff^{\mathrm{mirror}} \;=\; 7.447\left(\frac{T'}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4},
\]
and the Planck cap requires $T'/T_{\gamma} < 0.448$ (three relativistic mirror neutrinos; if the heaviest is non-relativistic at recombination, true for $T'/T_{\gamma}$ below about $0.3$ at our masses, the coefficient is $6.40$ and the threshold $0.47$; the paper carries the conservative figure). A copy releases the same entropy as ours at the same epochs, so this ratio is the ratio \emph{seeded at the descent} (the copied history fails at the mirror's nucleosynthesis near the floor, where burning reheats its plasma by $3.0$ to $3.2$, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}; the bound is met on either reading, by eight orders or more up to the hot-deposit point estimate of that Proposition): route (a) below does not arise for the mirror, and the descent must have heated it to less than $0.448$ of the visible temperature, the standard requirement of mirror-matter cosmology \cite{FootMirror2004}. The structure meets it with one datum: after the descent the mirror is heated only through the shared metric (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), which puts its temperature at a floor of about three parts in ten thousand of ours at the top of the ceiling range (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}(ii); $1.1 \times 10^{-3}$ even for a coefficient of ten, beyond the mirror's content), and above the floor the deposit sets it, near four parts in a thousand on the paper's estimate (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}). A cold mirror with our baryon number is what the framework predicts once that seeded temperature is taken as a free datum of the descent; by Proposition \claimref{dark-tower-matter.mirrors-temperature-p2} this is an exception to P2, which, applied with the reach of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv), (v), gives $T'/T_{\gamma} = 1$ and $\Delta\Neff = 7.45$, excluded by the cap above.

\emph{The five-dimensional towers.} A massless abelian species surviving in tower $r$ at temperature $T_{r}$ with $g_{r}$ light polarisations contributes
\[
\Delta\Neff \;=\; g_{r}\,\frac{4}{7}\left(\frac{11}{4}\right)^{4/3}\left(\frac{T_{r}}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4} \;\approx\; 2.2\,g_{r}\left(\frac{T_{r}}{T_{\gamma}}\right)^{4}
\]
($g_{r} = 2$ for a four-dimensional photon or a five-dimensional zero mode, $3$ if a fifth component is light). The cap $\Delta\Neff \lesssim 0.3$ is met by one such species if and only if $T_{r}/T_{\gamma} \lesssim (0.3/2.2\,g_{r})^{1/4}$, that is, $0.51$ for $g_{r} = 2$ and $0.46$ for $g_{r} = 3$, and by several jointly if their sum is under the cap.

Three routes close a channel, none proved here. (a) The sector is colder than the photons by a factor of about two, as a sector decoupled and releasing less entropy than ours is: the visible entropy release from the GeV epoch to today heats the photons relative to such a sector by $(g_{*}(\mathrm{GeV})/g_{*}(\mathrm{now}))^{1/3} \approx 2.51$, giving $\Delta\Neff \approx 0.11$ per two-polarisation species, so the two five-dimensional towers sit at $0.22$ with two light polarisations each, under the cap, and at $0.33$ with three, over it; a sector decoupled since the descent is colder still. (b) The abelian factor is Higgsed by the tower's own condensate, whenever that condensate carries the charge (this tower's neutral condensate is the accident that leaves our photon massless). (c) The rung-level charges, or the intrinsic $U(1)$, are not gauged in that tower once its content is derived as this tower's was. Route (a) is a thermal-history computation, (b) and (c) content derivations; all three are successor problem (1).

Observation level; the stance $\Delta\Neff \approx 0$ is registered conditional on them and on the mirror's seeded temperature.
proof: The mirror's relativistic content is a copy of ours (by \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so its total is the photon value plus the three-neutrino value $3.044$ (the record's Standard-Model $\Neff$); the threshold is $(0.3/7.447)^{1/4}$, script-bracketed. The single-species $\Delta\Neff$ formula is the ratio of the species' energy density to one neutrino species', $g_{r}/2$ times the two-polarisation value times $(T_{r}/T_{\gamma})^{4}$; the thresholds are its inversion, script-bracketed. The entropy-release factor is the standard $g_{*}^{1/3}$ scaling, $(61.75/3.91)^{1/3} \approx 2.51$ from the GeV epoch to today, and $4.40 \times 2.51^{-4} \approx 0.11$, script-bracketed. Routes (b) and (c) are stated, not proved. The seeded temperature rests on Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}, which supplies that after the descent the mirror couples to this tower only through the shared metric.

title: The ceiling valued, and an inherited success
text:
The families paper's alignment gives, within each sector, one vacuum direction and hence one rank-one Dirac mass at leading order \cite[Prop.~4.3]{ButlerT13}; it never equates magnitudes across sectors. This paper adds its own hypothesis, attacked below: \emph{Hypothesis (U)}, that the rank-one eigenvalues of the different sectors coincide at the ceiling, so that the neutrino's Dirac eigenvalue $m_{D}$ there is the common leading-order value, which the top retains and the second-order breaking splits for the down-type and charged-lepton sectors. With $m_{3}$ the heaviest light neutrino mass, the seesaw $m_{3} = m_{D}^{2}/M_{R}$ then values the scale on which two results depend, in a range whose ends are the two readings of (U):
\[
\frac{m_{b}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\approx\; 3.5 \times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{GeV} \;\lesssim\; M_{\mathrm{rung}} \;=\; M_{R} \;=\; \frac{m_{D}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\lesssim\; \frac{m_{t}^{2}}{m_{3}} \;\approx\; 6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{GeV},
\]
the upper end if the neutrino's Dirac mass is retained unbroken like the top's, the lower if it is split like the bottom's, with (U) read at a common low scale (read at the ceiling, the running of $m_{t}$ and $m_{b}$ lowers both ends by about an order of magnitude, a systematic the range does not include); the ends differ by $(m_{t}/m_{b})^{2} \approx 1.7 \times 10^{3}$, and which applies is a condensate-component question the families paper leaves open. Conditional on (U) and flagged so; (U) is used in two results, the $M$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-one-how-fragile}(ii) and the rung scale of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}(4). The same hypothesis puts the bottom and tau masses equal at the ceiling; whether their running reproduces the observed ratio near three is imported from the Standard-Model paper's run \cite{ButlerT12} at assembly level, a check to be passed, not one passed here.
proof: The valuations are division under (U), applied to the rank-one leading-order eigenvalues the alignment gives within each sector (\claimref{families.alignment-computed-thirteenth-refutation-democracy-one}): with $m_{t} \approx 173$ GeV, $m_{b} \approx 4.18$ GeV and $m_{3} \approx 0.05$ eV the heaviest light neutrino mass (the record's atmospheric splitting read as a mass), $m_{t}^{2}/m_{3} \approx 6 \times 10^{14}$ GeV and $m_{b}^{2}/m_{3} \approx 3.5 \times 10^{11}$ GeV; the script verifies both as exact rational bounds, $5 \times 10^{14} < m_{t}^{2}/m_{3} < 7 \times 10^{14}$ and $3 \times 10^{11} < m_{b}^{2}/m_{3} < 4 \times 10^{11}$ for the stated input brackets, and the ratio of the ends. The conditionality is Hypothesis (U) (\claimref{dark-matter.hyp-u-equal-rank-one-eigenvalues}), named in the statement and attacked in the section ``The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper''.

title: Parallel boundary mode spaces at one wall: the infall computation
text:
Matter of any tower crossing this tower's horizon meets the shared singular locus, which degenerates every tower's algebra, so each tower ascends its own ladder there, parallel boundary mode spaces at one wall. The fate of what fell in, for all towers and holes (clause (iii) limited in mass):

(i) \emph{Energy:} its rest energy joins the one metric (P1) and is returned democratically as Hawking radiation into every populated tower, in proportion to each tower's light degrees of freedom once the temperature exceeds their gaps, because barriers, transmission coefficients and occupancies belong to the exterior metric, which does not record which tower the mass came from; this is P1 with Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.frozen-phase-operators} and the Hawking paper's greybody assembly under its interface premise, run tower by tower \cite[Assembly~5.4]{ButlerT7}. (ii) \emph{Information:} it ascends its own tower's boundary mode space and returns in its own tower's channel, at little entropy cost: a solar-mass hole's Bekenstein entropy is of order $10^{77}$ against its progenitor's $10^{58}$, so the singularity paper's deficit theorem and Page curve are untouched, tower by tower. (iii) \emph{Gauss-law charges,} for holes below about $1.3 \times 10^{5}$ solar masses, are returned per tower by that tower's own discharge (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-schwinger-discharge-charged-hole}), at a cost of order the charge times the lightest charged mass, negligible against $M$; above that mass discharge does not limit the charge, and whether a supermassive hole returns it is left open here; no other clause uses (iii).

(iv) \emph{Global charges} are not returned in any tower, ours included (P5): information is returned at little cost because Hawking quanta are soft, and charge would cost the hole's mass to return because its lightest carrier is a GeV proton against a nanokelvin $T_{\mathrm{H}}$. (v) \emph{No remnant:} the singularity paper's exhaustiveness clause, imported as Fact \claimref{singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs-l-u} at its level there, a premise.

The late-stage evaporation therefore dims the visible final burst by the ratio of the total light degrees of freedom to the visible ones, of order the tower count if the towers are comparable, a minor prediction for primordial-black-hole burst searches at observation level, unconditional on the charge regime since it follows from (i) alone. The charge-saturated case is clearest: a hole formed from mirror matter alone has $Q_{2}m_{2} = M$, and it does not return its charge, exactly as no astrophysical hole of this tower returns ours. The ascend-then-descend structure at the degenerate locus is imported from the singularity paper \cite{ButlerT5}.
proof:
The shared locus: the metric is one (P1, \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}), so its degeneration locus is one, and at it each tower's Clifford bundle meets its own corank condition; the ascent is within-tower (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}), so each tower's boundary mode space opens separately over the same wall. Superselection (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}) constrains frozen-phase local operators, not counts: a mirror star collapsing and the hole radiating into every tower involves no operator with matrix elements between residues, the rest energy going into the shared metric and the emitted quanta being pair-created from each tower's own vacuum by that metric, the one channel Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable} leaves open; the clause that the four-dimensional boundary mode space cannot hold the superselected charge stays true and stays about the residue label.

(i) is the greybody assembly (\claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise}) applied per tower, with democracy following from the metric's insensitivity to the residue. (ii) is arithmetic the script brackets: $S_{\mathrm{BH}} = 4\pi G M^{2}/\hbar c$ at one solar mass against a few nats per baryon over $1.2 \times 10^{57}$ baryons, ratio of order $10^{-19}$. (iii) is Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-schwinger-discharge-charged-hole}, with that Fact's mass range. (iv) is P5 (\claimref{dark-matter.p5-boundary-modes-hold-entropy-not}), whose arithmetic the script brackets: the mass at which $T_{\mathrm{H}} = m_{p}$, $M_{\mathrm{Pl}}^{2}/(8\pi m_{p})$, in GeV and in grams, the maximal number of baryons a hole of that mass can emit, $M/m_{p}$, against the $M_{\odot}/m_{p}$ swallowed, and their ratio, below $10^{-20}$. (v) is the imported clause (Fact \claimref{singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs-l-u}).

Three consequences hold without changing any other result: the entropy accounting closes under democracy because the Hawking quanta are soft; the count is untouched, mass in holes still gravitating; and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}'s ``cannot be produced afterwards'' concerns production, holes being a permitted sink. The trichotomy for what fell in (exact charge return, democratic emission, no remnant) is decided by P5 against the first alternative, which would cost the Hawking paper's interface premise or the singularity paper's exhaustiveness. The dimming factor is greybody counting at observation level, the towers' degree-of-freedom counts not derived.

title: The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule
The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule
text:
Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent} derives one share of the survey ratio, the mirror's, and leaves the four odd towers' shares to a coupling rule the series does not supply (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}); that those towers are populated at all is the inference of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-are-populated}. This section states one rule that returns the remainder as a closed form, and says what the rule assumes, what mechanism returns its one length, and what the geometry of the series does and does not fix about it. The rule is a reading of the sourcing rule of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} with three premises added, at observation level throughout; it is not a coupling rule. The standing of the result is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness} and Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}.

\emph{A note on placement.} The unit-ball rule was proposed by the author after the first version of this paper was complete, and it was added as a section of its own, after the audits, rather than worked through the earlier sections, so that no result numbered in Sections 2 to 6 would move and every citation of them from elsewhere in the series would stay valid. It therefore reads as an addition to the paper. It is not a peripheral one: the rule is the paper's central quantitative result, the step that carries the derived mirror share through to the full dark-to-baryon ratio.

\emph{The number to explain.} With the mirror's share one (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(i)), the ratio is
\begin{equation}
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; 1 + 2 f_{3\mathrm{D}} + 2 f_{5\mathrm{D}}, \qquad f_{3\mathrm{D}} := f_{1} = f_{7}, \quad f_{5\mathrm{D}} := f_{3} = f_{5},
\end{equation}
where in this section $f_{r}$ is the share of the tower of residue $r$, its matter per unit of our volume in units of ours (not the asymmetric tower factor of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}, which vanishes for odd $r$), and the two equalities are P2's audit along the reversal orbit, which exchanges $1$ with $7$ and $3$ with $5$. The comparison throughout is with the Planck 2018 column that includes temperature, polarisation, low-$\ell$ polarisation and lensing, $0.1200/0.02237 = 5.364 \pm 0.065$ \cite{Planck2018}; the same paper's other columns give $5.376$ without lensing and $5.322$ with baryon acoustic oscillations, and the ACT DR6 combination with Planck, lensing and DESI gives about $5.22$ \cite{ACTDR6}. Agreement to more than two decimals is agreement with one column's rounded central value and carries no weight beyond $\pm 0.065$. The number to explain is $4.36 \pm 0.07$ from the four odd towers.

title: The nesting
text:
$\B^{n} \subset \R^{n}$ is the unit ball, $\Sph^{k} = \partial\B^{k+1}$ the unit sphere, $V_{n}$ the volume of $\B^{n}$ and $|\Sph^{k}|$ the area of $\Sph^{k}$, all Euclidean. A Lorentzian ``unit ball'' is not compact, so nothing that depends on signature enters, and a tower and its signature-reversed partner have the same measures, consistent with the pairing in the relation displayed with \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

Every tower shares this world's time and spatial directions as far as its signature allows (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}), its space being that of its representative under P3. A five-dimensional tower has one more spatial direction than ours; a three-dimensional tower has one fewer. So the towers' spaces nest in two chains, one through this world and one through the mirror:
\[
(1,2) \subset (1,3) \subset (1,4), \qquad (2,1) \subset (3,1) \subset (4,1),
\]
residues $7 \to 6 \to 5$ and $1 \to 2 \to 3$, each inclusion the hyperplane on which one coordinate vanishes. The two chains are exchanged by signature reversal, which is why the residue-$3$ tower, whose space contains the mirror's rather than ours, carries the same share as the residue-$5$ tower. a figure of the original shows the two chains as nested spaces, with the two sterile towers in their places. a figure of the original superimposes them: signature reversal is a reflection, so the two chains are the same shapes with the same measures about one centre, in one metric, and only the names change side, each tag in the figure naming the tower on its side.

title: The nesting
proof: (i) The generators square to the diagonal of the smaller signature and anticommute pairwise, so the inclusion of the smaller quadratic space extends to an injective algebra map (\claimref{std-algebra.functoriality}); the script checks all relations in $\Cl(1,4)$, $\Cl(1,3)$, $\Cl(4,1)$ and $\Cl(3,1)$ with \texttt{GA.py}. (ii) and (iii): a point with one coordinate zero has the same Euclidean norm in the smaller space.

title: The rule
text: The rule is stated inside the sourcing rule of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}: the one metric is the four-dimensional one, a tower shares this world's three spatial directions and its time, and the tower's contribution to the metric's source is its energy per unit of the shared three-volume, its content taken homogeneous along every direction it has. Three premises are added. None is supplied by the series.

title: The rule
text:
The balls the rule uses. With the standard closed form
\[
V_{D} \;=\; \frac{\pi^{D/2}}{\Gamma\!\left(\frac{D}{2} + 1\right)}, \qquad \Gamma(2) = 1, \quad \Gamma\!\left(\tfrac{5}{2}\right) = \frac{3\sqrt{\pi}}{4}, \quad \Gamma(3) = 2 :
\]
\begin{center} \begin{tabular}{clcccc}
\toprule
$D$ & world & its space & $V_{D}$ & value & $\dfrac{V_{3}}{V_{D}}$ \\[6pt]
\midrule
$2$ & the three-dimensional towers, residues $7$ and $1$ & a disc & $\pi$ & $3.142$ & $\tfrac{4}{3} = 1.3333$ \\[3pt]
$3$ & this world and the mirror, residues $6$ and $2$ & a ball & $\tfrac{4\pi}{3}$ & $4.189$ & $1$ \\[3pt]
$4$ & the five-dimensional towers, residues $5$ and $3$ & a four-ball & $\tfrac{\pi^{2}}{2}$ & $4.935$ & $\tfrac{8}{3\pi} = 0.8488$ \\[3pt]
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The share falls with dimension because the unit ball's volume grows from $D = 2$ to $D = 4$ (it peaks at $D = 5$), and one quantum per unit ball is then a lower density.

title: The unit-ball rule
text:
Under R1 to R3, the share of a tower whose space has $D$ dimensions is $f = \tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{D}}$, and
\[
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} \;=\; V_{3}\sum_{\text{dark }r}\frac{1}{V_{D_{r}}}
\;=\; \frac{V_{3}}{V_{3}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}} + 2\,\frac{V_{3}}{V_{4}}
\;=\; 1 + \frac{8}{3} + \frac{16}{3\pi} \;=\; \frac{11\pi + 16}{3\pi} \;=\; 5.36432\ldots
\]
against the observed $5.364 \pm 0.065$. The agreement is built in, not predicted: the relation was found by solving for the observed value, and its clauses were chosen with it known, and the closed form is one of fourteen equally simple candidates within the error bar (Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}).
proof:
The dark towers are the five of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(ii): the mirror, two three-dimensional and two five-dimensional. By R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}) the number density of the tower of residue $r$ in its own space is $1/V_{D_{r}}$ in the common unit, and by R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) its mass density is
\[
\rho_{r} \;=\; \frac{m}{V_{D_{r}}}, \qquad \rho_{\mathrm{us}} \;=\; \frac{m}{V_{3}}.
\]
By R3 (\claimref{dark-matter.r3-one-cell-per-unshared-direction}) that density counts per unit of our three-volume without a further factor: a five-dimensional tower's density per unit four-volume, taken through one unit of the extra direction, is a density per unit three-volume; a three-dimensional tower's density per unit area, with sheets one unit apart, is a density per unit three-volume. Ours is $\rho_{\mathrm{us}}$, the mirror's too. Divide; $m$ cancels. The values are those of the table:
\[
\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}} \;=\; \frac{4\pi/3}{\pi} \;=\; \frac{4}{3}, \qquad
\frac{V_{3}}{V_{4}} \;=\; \frac{4\pi/3}{\pi^{2}/2} \;=\; \frac{8}{3\pi}, \qquad
1 + 2(1.3333) + 2(0.8488) \;=\; 5.3643 .
\]
The script evaluates the closed form in $(5.36431, 5.36433)$ by rational bounds on $\pi$.

title: Why the ball is in the denominator
text: The share is a ratio of densities, not of sizes. One quantum per unit ball is a density of $\tfrac{1}{V_{D}}$, so a tower with a larger cell has its one quantum spread over more volume and is filled more thinly: the three-dimensional towers' disc ($3.14$) is smaller than our ball ($4.19$), so their filling is denser and their share exceeds one; the five-dimensional towers' four-ball ($4.93$) is larger, so their filling is sparser and their share is below one. The opposite reading, share proportional to the cell, would say that a larger world holds more matter, which is right for total mass at equal density but is not what gravity in our world sees (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}); it gives $\tfrac{3}{4}$ and $\tfrac{3\pi}{8}$ and a total of $4.856$, excluded at more than seven standard deviations.

title: What the rule has and has not
text: One rule is applied identically to every tower, our world entering once, as $V_{3}$, in every comparison, so every share is a multiple of the one $\Omega_{b}$ gravity measures; there is no distinction between towers we contain and towers that contain us, and no observer in another tower would compute a different $\rho_{r}/\rho_{\mathrm{us}}$, because the rule is Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} with the thickness R3 states. What the rule does not have is a reason for R1 or R2: R1 is consistent with the series' mass formulas (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.r1-against-series-mass-formulas}) but not derived; R2 asks every tower to be filled at the same spacing, which for this tower is set by baryon number, a charge the odd towers do not carry (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}). R3 is a length, fixed at one cell radius; the section ``The thickness: a contact mechanism'' gives a mechanism that returns that value and costs it. The rule is not the coupling rule of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}: it says nothing about the odd towers' scales, lightest states or number-changing rates, only how much of their matter, whatever it is, sources our metric per unit of our volume.

title: The extra direction must co-expand
text: R2 defines one spacing in every direction of each tower's own space, and the spacing grows with the scale factor. If the extra direction were static, a case Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} allows, the spacing along it would stay fixed while the spacing along the shared directions grew, so R2 could hold at one epoch only; under the lemma the projected density would still dilute as $a^{-3}$ and the ratio would stay constant, but at a value that is the rule's at one epoch alone. So R2, held at all times, selects the co-expanding case, and today the extra direction is about one baryon spacing, of order a metre comoving, growing with the universe. This is a cost of R2, not of the value R3 gives.

title: Equivalent forms, and an assignment that is not
text:
Archimedes' hat-box identity \cite{Archimedes},
\[
|\Sph^{n+1}| \;=\; 2\pi\,V_{n}
\]
(the uniform measure on $\Sph^{n+1}$, projected onto $\R^{n}$ by forgetting two coordinates, is $2\pi$ times the uniform measure on $\B^{n}$; script-checked for $n = 0$ to $6$), gives $|\Sph^{3}| = 2\pi^{2}$, $|\Sph^{4}| = \tfrac{8\pi^{2}}{3}$ and $|\Sph^{5}| = \pi^{3}$. Hence R2 is equivalent to one quantum per unit sphere $\Sph^{n}$, $n = D + 1$, of each tower's spacetime, up to a universal factor $2\pi$ that cancels, and in that form
\[
f_{3\mathrm{D}} = \frac{|\Sph^{4}|}{|\Sph^{3}|} = \frac{4}{3}, \qquad f_{5\mathrm{D}} = \frac{|\Sph^{4}|}{|\Sph^{5}|} = \frac{8}{3\pi}, \qquad
\frac{\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}}{\Omega_{b}} = |\Sph^{4}|\sum_{\text{dark }r}\frac{1}{|\Sph^{n(r)}|},
\]
with $n(r)$ the tower dimension of residue $r$ and each world's sphere the equator of the next world's (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(iii), a figure of the original). A third assignment, our world as the ball $\B^{4}$ towards a tower we contain and as its boundary $\Sph^{3}$ towards a tower that contains us, $f_{3\mathrm{D}} = \tfrac{V_{3}}{V_{4}}$ and $f_{5\mathrm{D}} = \tfrac{|\Sph^{4}|}{|\Sph^{3}|}$, gives the same two numbers on the opposite towers, and so the same total. It is not physically consistent. Our own density stands in the denominator of every share, and by Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} it is one quantity, our mass per unit of our three-volume; this assignment reads our world as a volume in one comparison and as a surface in the other, and so gives our own density two values at once, which one metric cannot see. It is not a mechanism, since no rule can count our own density two ways (script: no fixed divisor with unit regions reproduces that pair in that order), and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness} shows it is the family at thickness $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, the arc of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-roots-are-chord-arc-quarter} in place of the flat chord that R2's cells have. So the ball and sphere forms are one rule, the factor $2\pi$ cancelling, while the exchanged assignment agrees with them in the total only. The two differ in composition: under the rule dark matter is $18.6\%$ mirror, $49.7\%$ three-dimensional and $31.6\%$ five-dimensional, and under the exchanged assignment the last two are exchanged. The total cannot tell them apart, and that difference is what the galaxy-cluster tests of the section ``The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy'' probe. Read at composite strength (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}), the colliding share of the dark matter, the mirror's included, is $68\%$ under the rule and $50\%$ under the exchanged assignment, and both fail the Bullet Cluster and the shapes of galaxy clusters. With the odd towers' matter collisionless both collide only the mirror's $18.6\%$, and those tests cannot separate them. Either way the choice between the two rests on the consistency argument above, not on the clusters.

title: The thickness: a contact mechanism
text:
R3 is a premise: it fixes the thickness at one cell radius, on one side, and nothing in the series does. This subsection gives a mechanism that returns that value. The count is made in the towers' own spaces, by asking which quanta of a tower are in contact with a world whose space is a slice of the tower's, the count being made on the nested world's space and carried to the containing world's by reciprocity. The mechanism has four clauses on how cells make contact. They were chosen with the value known, each has a stated alternative that the observation excludes (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}), and the mechanism holds for one nesting at a time and does not compose across two (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.scope-mechanism}). So what follows explains R3's value and does not derive it, and the tier of the rule is unchanged. The one-parameter family in which the thickness is a parameter is recorded afterwards as the sensitivity analysis. Throughout, $d_{b}$ is the common spacing of R2, the Wigner-Seitz radius, lengths are in units of it, a quantum's \emph{cell} is the ball of radius one about it in its tower's space, and a count is \emph{downward} when a world counts the cells of the tower whose space contains its own.

\emph{The four clauses.} (C) Contact: a quantum sources a world whose space is a slice of its tower's exactly when its cell meets that slice. (I) Indivisibility: a quantum that sources a world counts whole, its mass $m$ and not a fraction of it set by how much of its cell the slice cuts. (S) The side: across the direction a nesting adds or lacks, sourcing runs on one side only, the side named by the sign of the central volume element $\omega$ of the odd member of the nesting, whether that member is the tower counted or the world counting; where the odd member has two modules (residues $1$ and $5$) each module names a side, and a sheet of the three-dimensional tower holds one module. (O) Reciprocity: the ratio of two nested towers' densities found by the downward count on the nested world's space is the ratio read on the containing world's space. S postulates the side; Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algebra} only says what a side is. O is the equality of R3's two thicknesses in another form (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}(iii)).

title: The direction a nesting adds, in the algebra
text:
Write $P$ for the even world's pseudoscalar, the ordered product of its generators, and $\omega$ for the central volume element of the odd tower. In the four nestings of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(i):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Residue $5$, $\Cl(1,4) \supset \Cl(1,3)$.) $\omega = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}e_{4}$ is central with $\omega^{2} = +1$, $P = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$ has $P^{2} = -1$, and the fifth direction is
\[
e_{4} \;=\; P^{-1}\omega .
\]
Reversing our orientation, $P \mapsto -P$ with $\omega$ fixed, reverses $e_{4}$. The central idempotents $\tfrac{1}{2}(1 \pm \omega)$ cut out the two simple components on which the two irreducible modules live (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}(iv)), and $e_{4}$ acts on them as $\pm P^{-1}$. The reflection through our world, $x_{4} \mapsto -x_{4}$, fixes $P$ and sends $\omega \mapsto -\omega$: it exchanges the two components.
\item[(ii)] (Residue $3$, $\Cl(4,1) \supset \Cl(3,1)$.) The mirror's algebra is the slice $\{e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{4}\}$ with $P = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{4}$, $P^{2} = -1$; $\omega^{2} = -1$, one module; the added direction is $e_{3} = -P^{-1}\omega$, reversed by $P \mapsto -P$.
\item[(iii)] (Residue $7$, $\Cl(1,2) \subset \Cl(1,3)$.) $\omega = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}$ is central in the slice with $\omega^{2} = -1$, and the direction the three-dimensional tower lacks is $e_{3} = \omega^{-1}P$.
\item[(iv)] (Residue $1$, $\Cl(2,1) \subset \Cl(3,1)$.) The slice is $\{e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{3}\}$, $\omega = e_{0}e_{1}e_{3}$ is central in it with $\omega^{2} = +1$, two modules, and the lacking direction is $e_{2} = -\omega^{-1}P$.
\end{enumerate}
These are identities: $\omega$ is the ordered product $P e_{4}$ (or $\omega_{3}e_{3}$), so each equation restates the ordering, and its sign under $P \mapsto -P$ is immediate. What they fix is the meaning of a side: given the even world's orientation, the sign of $\omega$ is the sign of the direction the nesting adds or removes. Where $\omega^{2} = +1$ (residues $5$ and $1$) that sign is a label a quantum carries, its simple component; where $\omega^{2} = -1$ (residues $3$ and $7$) $-\omega$ is the conjugate complex structure on the same real module, and the sign is a convention for the tower as a whole. The lemma supplies no half-space: that a quantum sources on the side its sign names is clause S.
proof: Direct computation in each slice of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(i), the minus signs in (ii) and (iv) coming from moving one generator past another; $e_{4}\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}(1 \pm \omega) = \pm P^{-1}\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}(1 \pm \omega)$ since $\omega(1 \pm \omega) = \pm(1 \pm \omega)$; the reflection $v \mapsto -e_{4}ve_{4}^{-1}$ fixes $e_{0}$ to $e_{3}$ and negates $e_{4}$. Centrality and the squares of $\omega$ are the centre computation in the proof of Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.type-residue-what-each-tower-can}. The script computes all of it in \texttt{GA.py}.

title: The contact mechanism returns R3
proof:
(i) Take coordinates on the five-dimensional tower's space $\R^{4}$ with our space the hyperplane $x_{4} = 0$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(ii)). By R2 (\claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}) the quanta's centres have density $1/V_{4}$ per unit four-volume. A cell, the unit ball about a centre at height $x_{4} = h$, meets the hyperplane exactly when $|h| \leq 1$ (C); each such quantum counts whole (I); and each sources on one side only (S), the side its sign of $\omega$ names through Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algebra}(i). Which side is immaterial to the number: the quanta of one sign source our world from the slab $0 \leq h \leq 1$ and those of the other from $-1 \leq h \leq 0$, and whether the tower holds both signs at half the density each or one sign at the whole density, the quanta sourcing our world per unit of our three-volume number
\[
\int_{0}^{1}\frac{dh}{V_{4}} \;=\; \frac{1}{V_{4}},
\]
one cell radius of the extra direction; with R1 (\claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum}) the density is $m/V_{4}$ against ours, $m/V_{3}$.

(ii) The contact count runs downward only. A cell of the containing tower is a solid region meeting the nested world's space in a region of positive measure, whereas the cells of a tower nested in this world are discs in a sheet, and no count of discs per unit of our three-volume is defined until the sheets' spacing is. So count on the three-dimensional tower's own space, the plane $x_{3} = 0$ in ours (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.nesting}(ii)), where our quanta are the containing tower's: their centres have density $1/V_{3}$ per unit three-volume, a cell meets the plane when $|x_{3}| \leq 1$, it counts whole, and each sheet is sourced from one side, the side named by the sheet's own $\omega$ across the direction it lacks (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.direction-nesting-adds-algebra}(iii) or (iv); at residue $1$ each module names a side, and S takes each sheet to hold one module, so a sheet of either kind is sourced from one side; a sheet holding both would be sourced from both, at $2/V_{3}$). Per unit area of the plane our quanta number $1/V_{3}$ and the tower's own $1/V_{2}$, so on that world
\[
\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{us}}}{\rho_{3\mathrm{D}}} \;=\; \frac{V_{2}}{V_{3}} .
\]
By O the same ratio holds read on our space, $\rho_{3\mathrm{D}}/\rho_{\mathrm{us}} = V_{3}/V_{2}$. A family of sheets $s$ apart, each of density $m/V_{2}$ per unit area, has density $m/(V_{2}s)$ per unit three-volume, so $s = 1$: the sheets are one cell radius apart, which is the sheet clause of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} with its unit named. The nestings over the mirror (residues $3$ and $1$) are not reached by the count, since the residue-$3$ tower's space contains the mirror's and not ours; $f_{3} = f_{5}$ and $f_{1} = f_{7}$ are P2's audit along the reversal orbit, as in the relation displayed with \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

(iii) (i) and (ii) are R3's two clauses with the value one cell radius. The unit is R2's: with any other cell convention the contact slab has another width (the mean spacing is $n^{-1/3} = 1.61\,d_{b}$, and cubic cells give the $5.000$ of the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress}). Two-sided contact gives $2/V_{4}$, so S is the factor one half. In (ii) the downward count fixes $\rho_{\mathrm{us}}/\rho_{3\mathrm{D}}$ on the sheet, and for sheets $s$ apart the ratio read on our space is $V_{3}/(sV_{2})$; O sets the two equal, which is $s = 1$, so O is the equality of the sheet spacing and the extra length. Every count is a number of quanta per unit region of radius $d_{b}$, so $d_{b}$ cancels in each ratio as $m$ does by R1. The script recomputes the slab count as an integral, the downward count, the total, the alternatives of the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}, and the non-composition of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.scope-mechanism}.

The section weighting counts a cut cell by the measure of its section relative to the maximal section, one normalisation among several: a unit $D$-ball cut at height $h$ has section measure $V_{D-1}(1 - h^{2})^{(D-1)/2}$, and relative to $V_{D-1}$ these weights integrate over both sides to $V_{D}/V_{D-1}$, which for $D = 4$ is $\tfrac{3\pi}{8}$, the $\cos^{4}$ factor of the zero-mode reduction (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-reductions}(i)); that reduction is the five-dimensional count with I and S withdrawn. With C withdrawn the sourcing rule reverts to the homogeneous integral over a length $c$, which is Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}. The list is the paper's, not exhaustive; other cell conventions and other normalisations of a partial count are not on it.}

title: What S uses, and what it does not
text: S needs a side for each sourcing quantum or sheet, and the side is postulated. What the lemma supplies is that a side exists: in an odd tower $\omega$ is central, so its sign is a label a quantum carries where the centre splits and a convention for the tower where it does not, and in the even neighbour's frame that sign is the sign of the direction the nesting adds; the even towers have no such sign, their centre being $\R$. S selects no module: where $\omega^{2} = +1$, Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mode-counts-two-modules-which-one}(ii) counts both modules under P2, R2 with S then puts each at half the density on its own side, and the two slabs sum to one cell radius, exactly as if one module held the whole density. Where $\omega^{2} = -1$ the sign is a convention for the tower, every quantum sources the same side, and the count is one cell radius at full density. S uses no orientation off the reversal orbit: reversing the neighbour's $P$ exchanges every side at once and the count is unchanged, so P1's orientation clause stays where Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} keeps it. And S does not orient the odd tower's family: Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension} concerns the flag bit, and the sign of $\omega$ is a different object. What is postulated is the one-sidedness itself, and for the residue-$1$ sheets the further stipulation that a sheet holds one module; without the first both sides count and the total is $5.729$ (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}), and without the second the residue-$1$ sheets are sourced from both sides.

title: Scope of the mechanism
text: Two limits keep the mechanism an explanation of R3's value rather than a derivation of it. First, it does not compose. For the double nesting of the three-dimensional tower's plane in the five-dimensional tower's space, R3 gives $\rho_{5\mathrm{D}}/\rho_{3\mathrm{D}} = V_{2}/V_{4} = 0.637$, one cell radius for each of the two unshared directions; counting the five-dimensional cells that meet the plane directly by C and I gives $V_{2}^{2}/V_{4} = 2$ on the full transverse disc, $1$ on a half-disc and $\tfrac{1}{2}$ on a quadrant, and S is undefined there, $P^{-1}\omega$ across two directions being a bivector. So C with I holds for adjacent nestings only, which is where the rule uses it, and O is not tested there; R3, which composes, is the statement, and the mechanism is a reading of one step. Second, C restricts the homogeneous integral of Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones} to one cell radius, and under it the five-dimensional tower's matter further from this world sources the one metric not at all. With P1 that matter is either absent, so that the extra direction is about one cell deep (the co-expanding direction of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.extra-direction-must-co-expand}, forced rather than allowed) and C adds nothing to the integral over it, which is R3; or present and inert to gravity, against Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.sourcing-rule-forced-not-chosen}(i), which takes the integral over the whole direction as the only covariant choice. On the first branch C is R3; on the second it contradicts a proposition the paper calls forced. On neither is it a foundation.

title: The thickness: a contact mechanism
text: \textbf{Sensitivity.} The rest of this subsection records the total's dependence on the thickness taken as a parameter, which is where the observation's constraint on R3 lives.

title: The total as a function of the thickness
proof:
Per unit of our three-volume (by Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}), with the common quantum mass of \claimref{dark-matter.r1-equal-mass-per-quantum} and one quantum per unit ball of \claimref{dark-matter.r2-one-quantum-per-unit-ball}, the three densities are
\[
\rho_{5\mathrm{D}} = \frac{m\,c}{V_{4}\,d_{b}^{3}}, \qquad
\rho_{3\mathrm{D}} = \frac{m}{c\,V_{2}\,d_{b}^{3}}, \qquad
\rho_{\mathrm{us}} = \frac{m}{V_{3}\,d_{b}^{3}},
\]
so the shares are
\[
f_{3\mathrm{D}} = \frac{V_{3}}{c\,V_{2}} = \frac{4}{3c}, \qquad f_{5\mathrm{D}} = \frac{c\,V_{3}}{V_{4}} = \frac{8c}{3\pi},
\]
and the sum, with the mirror's share $1$ from Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent} and two towers of each odd dimension, with equal shares within each odd pair (by \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}), is the relation displayed with \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}. (i) Substitute. (ii) $T$ is of the form $1 + \frac{A}{c} + Bc$ with $A = \frac{8}{3}$ and $B = \frac{16}{3\pi}$; by the arithmetic-geometric inequality
\[
\frac{A}{c} + Bc \;\geq\; 2\sqrt{AB}, \qquad \text{with equality at } c = \sqrt{\frac{A}{B}} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}} .
\]
(iii) $T(c) = T(1)$ is the quadratic
\[
Bc^{2} - \bigl(T(1) - 1\bigr)c + A = 0, \qquad c_{1}c_{2} = \frac{A}{B} = \frac{\pi}{2};
\]
$c = 1$ is a root by construction and $\frac{\pi}{2}$ is the other. (iv) and (v) are evaluation. The script checks (i) as an identity in $\pi$ for rational $c$, brackets $T_{\ast}$ and the window endpoints by rational bounds on $\pi$ and on the square root, and evaluates the fractions.

title: The two roots are the chord and the arc of a quarter turn
text: In the sphere form of the rule, represent the five-dimensional tower's spacetime by a sphere of radius $R$ with our spacetime as its equator. The region between the equator and one pole has extent $R$ along the polar axis (the chord) and $\tfrac{\pi R}{2}$ along the surface (the arc). With $R = d_{b}$: counting the tower's matter per unit chord over that region is the unit-ball rule, $c = 1$; counting it per unit arc is the exchanged assignment, $c = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$; and the two totals agree because Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(i) exchanges them, while their compositions differ (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}). R2 selects the chord: its cells are unit balls of the tower's flat space, whose measure along the added direction is the radius. Between the equator and both poles the values are $c = 2$ and $c = \pi$, giving $5.729$ and $7.182$, both excluded.
proof:
The chord from the equatorial plane to a pole is the radius; the arc is a quarter of a great circle. With both poles, in the total of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness},
\[
T(2) = 1 + \frac{4}{3} + \frac{32}{3\pi} = 5.729, \qquad T(\pi) = 1 + \frac{8}{3\pi} + \frac{16}{3} = 7.182 ;
\]
the script brackets both and confirms that each misses by more than four standard deviations. The clock reflection $r \mapsto 4 - r$, which exchanges each three-dimensional tower with a five-dimensional one, is the bookkeeping image of (i) and not a symmetry of the physics, the two odd types differing in gauge content and algebra type.

title: The common thickness, and the curve if the two differ
text:
R3 takes the extra length and the sheet spacing equal; in the mechanism that equality is clause O. Let them differ, $c_{5}$ and $c_{3}$. With $c_{5} = 1$ kept, the observation confines $c_{3}$ to $[0.976, 1.025]$ at one standard deviation and nothing else constrains it; with both free it fixes a curve,
\[
\frac{8}{3c_{3}} + \frac{16c_{5}}{3\pi} \;=\; 4.364,
\]
whose two intersections with the diagonal $c_{3} = c_{5}$ are the roots of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(iii), and off the diagonal nothing natural lands on it ($c_{3} = \tfrac{4}{3}$ needs $c_{5} = 1.39$, $c_{3} = 2$ needs $c_{5} = 1.79$).

title: What could fix the unit: the de Sitter reading
text: The rule needs one length common to all towers. The series fixes exactly one length, and this subsection follows it.

title: Imported: the frozen point and the de Sitter radius
text: On the Einstein region with $\Lambda > 0$ of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), the scale tractor $I$, parallel for the tractor gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, has squared norm $Q(I) = \tfrac{\Lambda}{3}$, its stabiliser is the de Sitter group $SO(1,4)$, its orthogonal complement $I^{\perp}$ in the vectors of $\Cl(2,4)$ carries the induced form of signature $(1,4)$, and the flat-model section is the de Sitter hyperboloid of radius $\ell$, $\ell^{2} = \tfrac{3}{\Lambda}$. Under the action as written, $\Lambda$ is a parameter of the laws, not initial data. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~4.7, Prop.~4.10, Prop.~4.4]{ButlerT6}; \cite[Fact~2.1, Thm.~3.1, Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT10}.
proof:
