title: The two reductions
text:
In the setting of $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$, read in five-dimensional Gauge Theory Gravity (the $d$-dimensional clause of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}): the warped product $\ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\,ds_{4}^{2}$ is the derived metric of the gravitational field on flat $\R^{4,1}$, in the signature $(-,+,+,+,+)$ of $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$ (in the store's sign the derived metric is its negative), with $\hb^{-1}(e_\theta) = \ell\,e_\theta$ and $\hb^{-1}(a) = \cos\theta\,\hb_{4}^{-1}(a)$ on the four-dimensional directions, and the five-dimensional Einstein-Hilbert action is $\int \det(\hb)^{-1}\,\mathcal{R}\,d^{5}x$ (sign as in $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Zero mode.) Integrating the five-dimensional Einstein-Hilbert and matter actions over $\theta$, the gravitational term, the bulk dust and the equatorial sheet acquire the factors
\[
\ell\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^{2}\theta\,d\theta = \frac{\pi\ell}{2}, \qquad
\ell\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^{4}\theta\,d\theta = \frac{3\pi\ell}{8}, \qquad 1,
\]
so $G_{4} = \frac{2G_{5}}{\pi\ell}$. Newton's constant cancels in the ratio, and the five-dimensional tower's effective thickness is
\[
L_{\mathrm{eff}} \;=\; \frac{3\pi}{8}\,\ell \;=\; \frac{V_{4}}{V_{3}}\,\ell .
\]
\item[(ii)] (Local projection.) For dust comoving with the slice, $T_{ab}n^{a}n^{b} = 0$ and $T = -\rho_{5}$, so the bulk term of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-induced-equations-hypersurface} contributes on the slice the energy density
\[
\frac{2\kappa_{5}^{2}}{3}\left(\rho_{5} - \frac{\rho_{5}}{4}\right) \;=\; \frac{\kappa_{5}^{2}\,\rho_{5}}{2} .
\]
With the $G_{4}$ of (i) this is an effective thickness $L_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\pi}{4}\,\ell$.
\item[(iii)] (The sheets.) A comoving family of three-dimensional sheets carrying total mass $M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ over our $\Sph^{4}$ of radius $\ell$, each at the three-dimensional tower's own density $\frac{M_{\mathrm{tot}}}{|\Sph^{3}|\,\ell^{3}}$, has spacing
\[
s \;=\; \frac{|\Sph^{4}|}{|\Sph^{3}|}\,\ell \;=\; \frac{4}{3}\,\ell
\]
along the polar arc.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, under D: (i) with (iii) gives every share $1$ and the total $5.000$; (ii) with (iii) gives $4.333$; (i) with sheets one radius apart gives $5.667$; (ii) with sheets one radius apart gives $5.000$ again (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.two-reductions}). The rule's $L_{\mathrm{eff}} = \ell$ is produced by neither reduction. \emph{Beyond one flat chart.} The closed four-sphere of radius $\ell$ over which the sheet family of (iii) is counted is global and is not carried by a single gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime; the statements above that hold on the invertible region are in Gauge Theory Gravity, and that four-sphere is read on the manifold assembled from the derived metric's charts.
proof:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric below is the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat $\R^{4,1}$, in the signature $(-,+,+,+,+)$ of $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$, and its index expressions are readings of $D$ and of the field strength through Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}.

The integrals are Wallis's. Foliating $\Sph^{n+1}$ by latitude $\phi$, the latitude sphere is an $\Sph^{n}$ of radius $\cos\phi$, so
\[
|\Sph^{n+1}| \;=\; |\Sph^{n}|\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^{n}\phi\,d\phi, \qquad \int\cos^{n} \;=\; \frac{n-1}{n}\int\cos^{n-2}, \qquad \int\cos^{0} = \pi, \quad \int\cos^{1} = 2,
\]
which give
\[
\int\cos^{2} \;=\; \frac{\pi}{2}, \qquad \int\cos^{3} \;=\; \frac{4}{3} \;=\; \frac{|\Sph^{4}|}{|\Sph^{3}|}, \qquad \int\cos^{4} \;=\; \frac{3\pi}{8} \;=\; \frac{V_{4}}{V_{3}}
\]
(script: the recursion and the three values as identities in $\pi$). (i) For the warped product $ds_{5}^{2} = \ell^{2}d\theta^{2} + \cos^{2}\theta\; ds_{4}^{2}, \qquad \theta \in (-\pi/2, \pi/2)$, $\sqrt{g_{5}} = \ell\cos^{4}\theta\sqrt{g_{4}}$ and the scalar curvature contains $\cos^{-2}\theta\,R_{4}$ plus terms independent of $g_{4}$, so the coefficient of $\sqrt{g_{4}}R_{4}$ is $\ell\int\cos^{2}$; a bulk density uniform in $\theta$ integrates with $\sqrt{g_{5}}$ to $\ell\int\cos^{4}$; a density $\rho_{\mathrm{us}}\delta(\ell\theta)$ on the equator integrates to $\rho_{\mathrm{us}}$. Both matter terms feed the same four-dimensional equation with the same $G_{4}$, so their ratio is
\[
\frac{3\pi\,\ell\,\rho_{5}}{8\,\rho_{\mathrm{us}}}.
\]
(ii) Contract the bracket of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-induced-equations-hypersurface} with $u^{\mu}u^{\nu}$, $u^{2} = -1$: the energy density is $\rho_{5} - \rho_{5}/4$. (iii) With $s$ the spacing, the family's mass is
\[
\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\frac{M_{\mathrm{tot}}}{|\Sph^{3}|\,\ell^{3}}\;|\Sph^{3}|\,\ell^{3}\cos^{3}\phi\;\frac{\ell\,d\phi}{s}
\;=\; \frac{4M_{\mathrm{tot}}\ell}{3s},
\]
which equals $M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ when $s = \tfrac{4}{3}\ell$. The consequences: under D (\claimref{dark-matter.d-democracy-total-mass}),
\[
\frac{\rho_{5}\,\ell}{\rho_{\mathrm{us}}} \;=\; \frac{|\Sph^{4}|}{|\Sph^{5}|} \;=\; \frac{8}{3\pi}, \qquad
f_{5\mathrm{D}}^{\mathrm{(i)}} \;=\; \frac{3\pi}{8}\cdot\frac{8}{3\pi} \;=\; 1, \qquad
f_{5\mathrm{D}}^{\mathrm{(ii)}} \;=\; \frac{\pi}{4}\cdot\frac{8}{3\pi} \;=\; \frac{2}{3};
\]
(iii) gives $f_{3\mathrm{D}} = 1$, and sheets one radius apart give $\tfrac{4}{3}$. The totals follow from the relation displayed with \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}; the script brackets each and its distance from the observation.

d_{b} \;=\; \left(\frac{3}{4\pi n_{b}}\right)^{1/3} \;\approx\; 0.98\ \mathrm{m}, \qquad \ell \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{3}{\Lambda}} \;\approx\; 10^{26}\ \mathrm{m},

title: A reduced response to gravity needs a supporting stress; the sheets move

Then (i) it carries the anisotropic stress $\sigma = (1 - g)\psi$, and no other value; (ii) that stress enters the field equations, so that with the other components' stresses $\Sigma$,
\[
\psi \;=\; \frac{\phi - 12\pi G a^{2}\Sigma/k^{2}}{1 + 12\pi G a^{2}\rho\,(1 - g)/k^{2}} .
\]
For a three-dimensional tower whose sheets are held fixed, $g = \sin^{2}\theta$ for a wavevector at angle $\theta$ to the missing direction (script: $k_{\perp}^{2}/k^{2}$), $\tfrac{2}{3}$ averaged over orientations, and the stress of (i) is that of a medium holding the sheets in place. title: The sheet family and the linear spectra
text: Two readings of the sheet family are excluded, one by symmetry and one by the record. Both readings need the stress the series does not have. The reading it does have, $g = 1$, returns in the same code the standard model's temperature, polarisation, lensing and matter power spectra to four decimal places for the rule's composition (the towers as a separate species at full response), so at linear order the rule's dark sector is the standard model's. title: A halo built from collisionless sheets is a cold-dark-matter halo
text: Beyond linear order the question is what the sheets do to a halo, and the answer is an argument, not a simulation. A particle of a three-dimensional tower has two velocities: its motion within its sheet, the tower's own dynamics, and the motion of the sheet, which by Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress} follows the normal component of gravity pointwise. The one constraint the sheets impose is that at a point of a sheet the normal velocity is single-valued, the sheet being a surface; in-plane velocities are whatever the tower's dynamics allows, and sheets may cross, nothing forbidding it and the sourcing rule already stacking them. Cold dark matter is the same object in all three directions: a single-valued velocity field on a three-dimensional Lagrangian sheet in phase space, multi-streaming only where Lagrangian patches cross. So the sheet family's phase space contains cold dark matter's, one direction treated exactly as cold dark matter treats all three and two directions treated more permissively; with cold initial conditions, which the seeding floor gives (the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows''), the in-plane motion is itself a cold single-valued flow and the two phase spaces coincide. The Lagrangian map of the sheet matter is then cold dark matter's at every order in collisionless dynamics, not only at the linear order a figure of the original checks, and a simulation of sheet-labelled particles against plain ones would integrate the same equations. Halo shapes, velocity structure and the pancake, filament and halo sequence are cold dark matter's. What can differ is what the sheets add. title: The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy
text: The rule fixes how much matter each tower holds, and with it how much of the dark matter collides: the mirror's $18.6$ percent, a plasma once ionised inside a halo (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}), and the three-dimensional towers' $49.7$ percent, at composite strength within their sheets. Counted as a bound on what a galaxy cluster loses in a merger, the two add, to $68$ percent; Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(v) counts the three-dimensional towers alone. The companion note T14b \cite{ButlerT14b} tests these amounts where dark matter's collisions show, with a multi-species simulation code, a Bullet-like merger of two galaxy clusters, the assembly of a galaxy cluster from eight progenitors and a semi-analytic model of the Milky Way, deposited with its code, run outputs and films. It takes the amounts as given and runs them in two readings: as this paper writes them, and with the odd towers' matter collisionless, so that only the mirror collides, and it runs the exchanged assignment of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not} in the same way, since the two assignments differ in composition and not in the total. Its results are imported here.

title: Imported: the composition simulated
text:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Quanta confined to a sheet scatter in two dimensions. Per unit of the mass gravity sees, the three-dimensional towers' matter at composite strength has a cross-section of $10^{8}$ to $10^{13}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$ in galaxy clusters, eight to thirteen orders of magnitude above the galaxy-cluster bounds, whatever its confinement scale: it is a fluid whose pressure acts within its sheets.
\item[(ii)] In the merger, with the three-dimensional towers' matter colliding, the subcluster's sheet fluid and mirror gas are held back with its gas, and with randomly oriented sheets the subcluster has no separate lensing peak. With the odd towers' matter collisionless, the subcluster keeps a lensing peak on its galaxies with its gas $355$ kpc behind, and its mass-to-light change, $0.82$, is consistent with the observed ratio $0.84 \pm 0.07$ \cite{Randall2008}, as cold dark matter's is; the cost is a puffier subcluster, with lensing contrast $4.7$ against cold dark matter's $7.5$.
\item[(ii$'$)] The exchanged assignment of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}, with the three-dimensional towers' matter colliding, fails in the same way: lensing contrast $1.1$, the subcluster's own mass $0.27$ of cold dark matter's, and galaxy-cluster ellipticity $0.49$ of cold dark matter's. With the mirror settled it is marginal, contrast $2.7$ and mass $0.44$.
\item[(iii)] In the assembled galaxy clusters, two seeds each, the projected ellipticity is $0.43$ of cold dark matter's with the three-dimensional towers colliding, both seeds below cold dark matter's, the sheet fluid forming a cored component rounder than the collisionless dark matter; with the odd towers' matter collisionless it is $0.77$, rounder, with one seed inside the range of the cold-dark-matter seeds, so not excluded.
\item[(iv)] In the Milky Way, the proton-only branch is excluded at the Sun. On the burning branch a helium mirror, cooling slowly and with helium-star supernovae giving $3.6$ to $7.3$ times our feedback per unit mass formed, fits the $2\sigma$ room for extra disk-like mass at the Sun under some normalisations of its gas, and fits the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass. With the consistent yield, extra disk-like mass at the Sun below $5\ M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$, or disk-like dark mass in the bulge volume below $1.7 \times 10^{9}\ M_{\odot}$, would exclude it. Neither has yet been made (the dark-matter paper's own refutation condition 6, the section ``The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper'', not the series' sixth refutation).

title: The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy
text:
What follows for this paper is that the amounts survive. With the odd towers' matter collisionless the composition passes the Bullet Cluster, under either assignment, and is not excluded by the shapes of galaxy clusters. Read at composite strength, as Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what} reads it, the composition fails both, and it fails them because of that self-interaction, not because of the amounts. That reading is a premise of T14b, not derived here or there: it is a statement about the three-dimensional towers' couplings and the strength with which their lightest stable state interacts, which the series does not fix (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}). The mirror's exposure is the same in both readings and is refutation item 6's: (iv) turns the dark-disk test into two measurements not yet made. The simulations are idealised, with one merger geometry, $80{,}000$ particles per merger and two seeds per galaxy cluster, and they compare compositions; their absolute numbers are not predictions.

\emph{The density the rule assigns excludes composite strength as well.} On a sheet the number per unit area and the expansion rate both fall as $a^{-2}$ in radiation domination, so for two-dimensional s-wave annihilation, $\sigma_{1}v = 2P/m$ with $P$ the absorption probability per encounter, the ratio of the annihilation rate to the expansion rate does not fall, and the depletion runs on logarithmically to the present. A symmetric relic annihilating at full strength, $P = 1$, into lighter states of its own tower, which a confining tower has (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}, the Goldstone clause), is left at about $3 \times 10^{-14}$ of the density R2 assigns; a relic whose number is fixed at the descent, interacting too weakly to annihilate, keeps it. This is an order-of-magnitude estimate at the mean density on R1 and R2, script-checked in floating point (the section ``Machine verification'', Part N). It does not say why the odd towers' matter is free; it says that the density the rule assigns, like the galaxy-cluster record, needs it to be nearly so.

title: The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper
The premises attacked, and what would refute this paper
text: Each premise gets its own attack, run in the series' manner: state the strongest case against, and report what survives.

title: P1 attacked: could there have been more than one descent, or more than one orientation?
text:
The case against the orientation clause: a flag is defined per rung (Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}) and every tower has rungs, so nothing in the algebra forbids each tower its own choice; the clause is a statement about the event, not the algebra. What survives: the choice is initial data of the descent (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.orientation-arrow-seventeenth-refutation}), a per-tower choice would be a second uncaused datum of one event, which P2 refuses, and the clause is used in exactly two places, neither of which fails without it: the internal statement of the fifteenth refutation (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.asymmetry-arrow-counted-fifteenth-refutation}), and the second route to Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v), whose first route is P2's audit. Withdraw the clause and (v) stands by the audit, P4 reverts to a premise for the mirror, and the count is unchanged. Off the reversal orbit the clause cannot reach: over $\C$ there is no signature, an identification of two towers' ambients is fixed only up to a group whose two components exchange the two families, and ``the one flag'' would be defined only up to the bit at issue; hence the scoping in Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}.

The case against the rest: nothing in the transport principle forbids multiple division events, and a multi-descent history would give each tower its own $\Lambda$, expansion and asymmetry, dissolving the count, the ratio and the universality at once. What survives: the vacuum theorem derives one frozen point per metric, and there is observationally one metric, a second gravity being excluded by the equivalence-principle tests \cite{ButlerT6}; and the dating Observation locates the descent at the origin, a later descent being a second big bang inside this one's classical era, for which the record shows nothing \cite[Obs.~7.4]{ButlerT12}. P1 is supported, not proved; a pre-descent theory of the freezing (the capstone's declared open problem) would settle it. Its reading as a sourcing rule (Lemma \claimref{dark-matter.projection-every-towers-content-dilutes-ones}) is a further choice inside P1, the one that makes the count and the audit consistent; a different rule would have to be stated and both re-run.

title: P2 attacked: is indifference a law?
text: The case against: indifference is a selection rule on initial data, exactly where the trichotomy locates the framework's freedom, and might forbid the very contingency initial data is. The response is the instrument's audit, inherited from the families paper: in every use in a proof indifference equates along exact symmetry orbits and refuses selections with no distinguished member, and never legislates the \emph{values} of genuine moduli ($N$, $\epsilon$, the bit), which it classifies as data; it constrains the \emph{shape} of the pre-descent state, not its \emph{coordinates}. Here P2 counts both irreducible modules where the centre splits (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mode-counts-two-modules-which-one}(ii)); it does not equate the asymmetries of towers off the reversal orbit, and it does not sterilise $r = 0$ by refusing a flag there, which would refuse every residue (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.flag-insensitive-residue-no-flag-level}). P2 is a principle with a record of successful use (the families' democracy, the fuzzy sphere's principality), not a theorem; its failure mode is refutation item 1.

title: P3 attacked: why the nearest dimension?
text: The case against: every residue has a causal member once the dimension is free (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(i)), so the count five belongs to one window, and P3 picks it. What survives: P3 reads P1 (one metric) as a minimality condition, each tower as close to the visible four as its residue allows, and it is the only natural window returning the two-sterile answer; clause (iii) records what every other window gives, so the dependence is exposed. What does not survive: any claim that the fixed-point coincidence $\{0, 4\} = \{r : r \equiv -r\}$ is structural; it belongs to the window. A derivation of tower dimension from the descent (the wall's dimension in the sheaf paper is where it would come from \cite{ButlerT4}) would retire P3.

title: P4 attacked: is the asymmetry democratic?
text: The case against was that the asymmetry per mode depends on the tower's charge structure, which differs by residue, and nothing equates functions of inequivalent structures. The attack succeeds, and P4 is scoped to what survives it: it is a theorem for the mirror (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(v), by the audit along the orbit or by the copy with P1's one orientation, the paper carrying both routes), void for the odd residues (Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow}: nothing there to be democratic about), and a premise only on the two-time fork. The declared remainder: what remains of P4 is not used in any proof the paper relies on.

text: The case against: the families paper supplies a direction and states that the magnitude was never its physical content, each sector carrying its own normalisation; and this paper needs the second-order breaking to depress the down-type and lepton eigenvalues relative to the up sector by $m_{t}/m_{b}$, where the families paper describes that breaking as what lifts the two light families. If (U) fails the ceiling is unvalued, not wrong: the rung scale becomes a free datum of the pre-descent theory, successor problem (2).

title: P5 attacked: must the boundary modes return every conserved quantum number?
text: The case against: the singularity paper's purity premise, written (U$_{\mathrm{T5}}$) here to keep it apart from Hypothesis (U) \cite[Premise~11.3(U)]{ButlerT5}, extends to every conserved quantum number of the infalling state, so the boundary mode space must return baryon number and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(iv) is false. What survives: (U$_{\mathrm{T5}}$) is purity of the state on $H_{L} \otimes H_{R}$, which says nothing about a global $\mathrm{U}(1)$ the Hamiltonian need not commute with at the wall, where the algebra degenerates and the rung $\mathrm{U}(1)$ of Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.where-flag-defined-what-it-carries} (argued, not proved) has no reason to survive the ascent; and, decisively, the alternative makes every stellar hole in our tower a remnant or a non-Hawking emitter, against the imported flux. Read the other way, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall} is a constraint on the series: exact return of global charge would force the Hawking paper's interface premise or the singularity paper's exhaustiveness to fail in the saturated regime. If the series ever promotes exact return to a theorem, P5 reverses and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall} with it; the count and the shares are insensitive to holes and do not move.

title: R1 to R3 and D attacked: the unit-ball rule's premises
text:
The case against R1 (equal mass per quantum): the odd towers' quanta are composites of sectors whose confinement scales the series does not derive (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}), so nothing fixes their mass to ours; a factor two either way in a quantum's mass is a factor two in that tower's share, and no closed form survives it. What survives: Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.r1-against-series-mass-formulas} shows the series' mass formulas, compared in one normalisation, do not contradict R1, and the closed form's agreement is evidence for R1 at exactly the strength of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(ii), one candidate in fourteen.

The case against R3 (one cell radius per unshared direction, one side): it is the one number the whole relation turns on, the geometry's two computations of it give $\tfrac{3\pi}{8}$ and $\tfrac{\pi}{4}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.two-reductions}), and no gravitational measurement can reach it (Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity}). The contact mechanism that returns it (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}) is open to the same attack one clause at a time: contact and indivisibility are a hard-ball picture that nothing in the series gives an odd tower's quanta, and under contact the tower's matter beyond one cell radius sources nothing (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.scope-mechanism}); the side is postulated, the sign of $\omega$ being a label with no reason to become a direction of sourcing (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.what-s-uses-what-it-does}); the contact count does not compose across two nestings; and reciprocity is the equal-thickness assumption restated. What survives: each clause has a computed alternative that the observation excludes (the table accompanying \claimref{dark-matter.contact-mechanism-returns-r3}), so the mechanism's choices are exposed rather than hidden; and the family's floor, $5.255$, holds whatever becomes of R3.

The case against D: it is P2 applied to inequivalent towers, exactly the equation P2's audit refuses (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}(c)). What survives: nothing in the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule'' rests on D; it is named as the one route by which the series' own length could enter, and it does not reach the observed value.

title: What would refute this paper
text:
Seven ways, each with its cost. Item 6 is the standing test, where the derivation meets the record and the record is already pressing; item 7 is its gravitational-wave form, unconditional in class and model-dependent in rate; item 2 is an unconditional running experiment; item 4 is bounded by the deposit interval; item 5 is conditional on an unsolved successor problem; items 1 and 3 are theory-internal risks. That the odd towers are empty, or that no consistent value of their relic densities supplies the remainder, does not refute this paper, which does not derive the remainder (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(iii)); the capstone carries both as conditions on the programme \cite{ButlerT17}. The unit-ball rule's own exposures follow the six and refute the rule, not the paper.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Exhibit caused, tower-distinguishing structure in the pre-descent state, and P2 fails where most depends on it: the mirror's equivalence to this tower and the family ordering fall together (this paper and the families paper share the weakness).
\item Detect dark matter directly or indirectly at any strength above the gravitational floor, and the superselection is breached: Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable} is refuted outright, and with it the exact stability, the gravity-only seeding, and both conditional null stances.
\item Break the superselection argument itself: find a frozen-phase local operator that changes signature. The stability guarantee goes, though not the population count.
\item Exhibit one exactly massless dark species at a temperature above the thresholds of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}, and the radiation audit fails against the measured $\Neff$. Within the interval of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number} an excess reads first as a deposit hotter than the paper's estimate, the deposit energy being a datum the framework does not fix; it refutes item 2 only above the cap's own limit on the deposit, $T'/T_{\gamma} = 0.448$ for the mirror, where a species must have been heated by something other than gravity.
\item Derive the tower dimensions from the descent and find a window other than P3's, and the count of causal residues moves with the census of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.towers-are-residues-single-clock-filter}(iii); the asymmetric share moves only if a new even causal residue appears at a dimension divisible by four (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}): the windows that make $r = 0$ and $r = 4$ causal do so at $(1,1)$ and $(1,5)$, which carry no bit, so on those windows the asymmetric share is unchanged.
\item \emph{The standing test.} Find the mirror's share other than one. Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one} makes it a theorem, so this refutes P2 for the mirror, the descent's single ceiling, or the charge reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}. With the remainder of the ratio underived, this is the one place the paper's derived content meets the record, and the record is already pressing on it.

\emph{Already in tension:} the share is $18.6$ percent of the dark matter in cold, dissipative mirror baryons, and the record's analysis of mirror dark matter's galactic structure allows at most $0.8\,\Omega_{b}$ at low mirror temperature \cite{RouxCline2020}, a fifth below the prediction, which is a quarter above it. That analysis rescales the mirror's baryon-to-photon ratio as $\eta' = \eta\,\beta/x^{3}$ and includes a helium mirror down to $x = T'/T = 10^{-3}$, which covers the hot end of the framework's interval; it does not include the interval's floor, where the framework's mirror, whose $\eta'$ runs from about $0.008$ to $26$, reaches forty billion times ours, and is helium throughout on the expected branch (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}), nor the supernova energy of helium stars, which the companion note T14b finds to be $3.6$ to $7.3$ times ours per unit mass formed \cite{ButlerT14b}.

The dark-disk test runs in two phases. In the \emph{diffuse phase} mirror gas accreted into a halo is shock-heated to the virial temperature and ionised, a fluid with a mean free path of order ten parsecs ($\sigma/m \sim 10^{8}\ \mathrm{cm^{2}\,g^{-1}}$); this is what the Bullet Cluster's bound on the subcluster's mass loss, about $23$ percent and inferred from the mass-to-light ratios, tests \cite{Randall2008}; read as a bound on the dark matter, $18.6$ percent passes, and simulated, a merger in which only the mirror collides gives a mass-to-light change of $0.82$, consistent with the observed $0.84 \pm 0.07$, as cold dark matter's is (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-composition-simulated}(ii)). Its radiative cooling time is of order ten gigayears at the virial radius and a gigayear or less inside the cooling radius, where $n \gtrsim 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, so, as with our baryons, the inner gas radiates its support within a Hubble time and the outer gas does not. In the \emph{settled phase} what cools forms a mirror disk or compact objects of total mass up to $\Omega_{b'} \approx \Omega_{b}$; a thin disk of the visible disk's mass, about $50\ M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ locally, exceeds the Gaia thin-dark-disk bounds of a few $M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ \cite{Schutz2018, Widmark2021} by an order of magnitude, so the settled phase must not be a thin disk. A thick or fragmented component, or mirror feedback holding gas in the diffuse phase, avoids the bound; fragmentation into compact objects is closed by the microlensing limits (compact objects at most $1$ percent of the halo from $1.8 \times 10^{-4}$ to $6.3\ M_{\odot}$ and $10$ percent up to $860\ M_{\odot}$ \cite{Mroz2024}) unless the objects form outside that window. The phase split, the star-formation efficiency, the settled gas's fate and whether helium composition delays settling are the model; the record's mirror-galaxy analysis \cite{RouxCline2020} models them with a rescaled $\eta'$ and a helium mirror at the hot end of the interval, not at its floor; Randall et al.'s mass-to-light ratios \cite{Randall2008} are the observation behind the mass-loss bound, and Clowe et al.'s offset \cite{Clowe2006} behind the lensing test. Model-dependent, so on the burning branch a tension and not an exclusion: this is the framework's one theorem-level dark-matter prediction, and it is at the edge of the record already. The companion note T14b models the settled phase in the Milky Way (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-composition-simulated}(iv)): the proton-only branch is excluded at the Sun, and the burning branch's helium mirror, cooling slowly and with helium-star feedback, is open at the Sun under some normalisations of its gas and in the bulge only if the bulge holds over twice the mirror's proportional share of its dark mass, so that either of two measurements not yet made would decide it. Neither measurement can yet be made from published results. The tightest Gaia bound on a thin dark disk, about $5\ M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{pc^{-2}}$ at $95$ percent \cite{Widmark2021}, holds only for scale heights of $50$ pc or less, and at the $100$ to $500$ pc the test needs the bound is weaker; the dynamical models of the bulge \cite{Portail2017} measure its dark mass, about $3.1 \times 10^{9}\ M_{\odot}$, as halo-like, and do not separate a disk-like part from the stars' mass-to-light ratio. The test therefore needs two analyses not yet made: a vertical-dynamics or phase-space-spiral analysis of Gaia data with a dark disk of that thickness, and a bulge model with a disk-like dark component. Until then the Galaxy test is registered, not run.
\item \emph{Dark neutron-star mergers.} The copy theorem makes the mirror sector baryonic, dissipative and at the proton mass, so it forms stars, and its neutron stars have our equation of state: the same maximum mass and the same tidal deformability $\Lambda(M)$. The prediction is a class of compact-binary mergers in the ground-based gravitational-wave band with component masses of one to two solar masses, $\Lambda$ in the range of ordinary neutron stars, and no electromagnetic counterpart at any depth or distance. Nothing in the standard model produces that class, and primordial black holes in the mass range have $\Lambda = 0$. The rate is model-dependent: the mirror sector is helium-dominated on the expected branch (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}) and helium star formation has no calibrated efficiency, so the natural expectation is within an order of magnitude of the visible binary-neutron-star rate, tens to hundreds per cubic gigaparsec per year, and the framework fixes the class and the deformability, not the number. GW190425, with no counterpart and its deformability unconstrained, is the class's example event. Refutation: a large sample of neutron-star-mass mergers whose counterpart fraction is consistent with an all-visible population bounds $\Omega_{b'}$ below $\Omega_{b}$ and refutes Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-share-assembled} as item 6 does; confirmation is a counterpart fraction well below the visible population's with $\Lambda$ consistent with our equation of state, which third-generation detectors will measure for hundreds of events.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{The unit-ball rule's exposures} (the section ``The dark matter ratio: the unit-ball rule''; these cost the rule and Premises R1 to R3, not the paper). (a) A combined measurement of $\Omega_{\mathrm{dark}}/\Omega_{b}$ settling below the floor $5.255$ of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(ii) by more than its error excludes every thickness at once; the ACT DR6 combination's $5.22$ is already there if it holds. (b) A sharper measurement leaving $c = 1$ outside the window of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(iv) excludes R3 and the mechanism behind it; one leaving both windows excludes the exchanged assignment too and leaves a fitted $c$ with no geometric name. (c) The self-interacting fraction (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.total-function-thickness}(v)): at composite strength it is about a half at $c = 1$, and simulated, that composition fails the Bullet Cluster and the shapes of galaxy clusters (the section ``The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy''); with the odd towers' matter collisionless the colliding fraction is the mirror's $18.6$ percent, the composition passes the merger and is not excluded by the shapes, and a colliding fraction measured well away from it excludes that reading whatever the total does. Under that reading the fraction no longer separates the rule from the exchanged assignment (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.equivalent-forms-assignment-not}). (d) The sheets' displacement (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.reduced-response-gravity-needs-supporting-stress}): if the three-dimensional towers' sheets are held fixed by a stress the series does not name, the linear spectra exclude them (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.sheet-family-linear-spectra}) and no thickness reaches $4.364$ from the five-dimensional towers alone; if they move, their halos are cold dark matter's when their matter is collisionless (Remark \claimref{note.dark-matter.halo-built-collisionless-sheets-cold-dark}) and a cored fluid at composite strength (the section ``The composition in galaxy clusters and in the Galaxy''), and their exposure is the fraction test of (c) and, on the deposit branch, an in-plane free-streaming cutoff. Against these stands the caveat of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(ii): the closed form is one of fourteen equally simple candidates in the error bar, found by solving for the target, so the value alone is not evidence; the floor is, and the fraction is evidence about the three-dimensional towers' couplings.

Stabilising two-time dynamics opens a fork onto an oriented Kleinian Standard Model (Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow}) with an asymmetric share of one: on the fork the asymmetric ratio is two on the two equalities Corollary \claimref{dark-matter.which-towers-can-carry-arrow} names as premises there. The fork is a theoretical one (two-time dynamics has no stable formulation on the record) and is carried as such.

Six open and one closed, numbered as in the capstone's inventory; its (0), the charge-saturated hole, is discharged by P5 and Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}.

(1) \emph{The odd towers' content:} the odd-dimensional Fock ideals, their mass formulas and gauge algebras, not used in any proof here, are to be established at their proved levels; the parity theorem and the seeding floor are this paper's (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.flag-bit-exists-exactly-tower-dimension}, the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows'').

(3) \emph{The coupling rule:} the relation between an odd tower's dimensionful coupling and this tower's at the ceiling, which nothing derived in the series supplies; it alone stands between Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.population-count-one-share-half-percent}(iii) and a computed contribution from the odd towers, and the unit-ball rule constrains it (the odd towers' densities per unit of our volume) without supplying it. Two questions travel with it as conditions on the programme: whether a tower can be populated at all without the flag bit, and whether any consistent value of the odd towers' relic densities supplies the remainder. One signpost, conditional on two antecedents this paper does not assert: if the remainder is the odd towers' and they are relics of the gravitational seeding of the section ``Seeding by gravity, and why no coupling rule follows'' rather than of the deposit, the yield's $T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}$ scaling and the requirement that the produced quanta be no heavier than the bath put $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ above about $2 \times 10^{12}$ GeV, excluding the lower end of the ceiling range, and the odd towers' lightest stable state near $10^{5}$ GeV at its top.

title: Imported: the massless-graviton production rate
text:
Dark matter produced from the Standard-Model plasma by massless graviton exchange has rate per volume
\[
R(T) \;=\; \frac{\alpha\,T^{8}}{M_{P}^{4}}, \qquad M_{P} = 2.435 \times 10^{18}\ \mathrm{GeV},
\]
the reduced Planck mass, with $\alpha = 1.9 \times 10^{-4}$, $1.1 \times 10^{-3}$, $2.3 \times 10^{-3}$ for one scalar, one fermion and one vector \emph{produced} species respectively, the sum over the Standard-Model bath being inside the coefficient, weighted as $4|\mathcal{M}^{0}|^{2} + 45|\mathcal{M}^{1/2}|^{2} + 12|\mathcal{M}^{1}|^{2}$ over its scalar, Weyl-fermion and vector degrees. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Bernal2018}, Eq.~(31), $R^{0}(T) = (3997\pi^{3}/663552000)\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$ for the scalar case, and Table I, the massless-graviton limit of that paper's massive spin-2 mediator. title: Seeding by gravity: the floor on a dark tower's temperature
text:
By exact superselection the towers interact only through the shared metric (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), so after the descent a dark tower can be heated only gravitationally; what the descent itself deposited in it (its charge, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, with whatever energy the deposit carried) is a datum, not a computation. Let the descent reheat this tower to $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ and let tower $r$, with $g_{d}$ light degrees of freedom that thermalise among themselves, be heated by graviton-mediated production from the visible plasma at rate per volume $\Gamma = c\,T^{8}/M_{P}^{4}$, with $c$ the sum of Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}'s per-species coefficients over the tower's light content. Then the produced comoving yield is
\[
Y \;=\; \frac{c\,T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}}{3\,\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}}, \qquad \kappa_{s} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi^{2}g_{*}}{90}}\;\frac{2\pi^{2}}{45}\,g_{s} \;=\; 145.3 \ \text{at } g_{*} = g_{s} = 100,
\]
its energy fraction at production is $4Y$, and the temperature ratio it alone would give is
\[
\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} \;=\; \Big(4Y\,\frac{g_{*}}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4} \;=\; 9.6 \times 10^{-4}\; c^{1/4}\Big(\frac{16}{g_{d}}\Big)^{1/4}\Big(\frac{T_{\mathrm{desc}}}{6 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{GeV}}\Big)^{3/4}
\]
for $g_{*} = g_{s} = 100$ at the reheating. This is a floor: the tower's bath cannot be colder, and it is hotter by whatever energy the deposit carried. The ratio thereafter evolves through the two sectors' separate entropy conservation, by
\[
\left(\frac{g_{d}^{\mathrm{seed}}}{g_{d}}\right)^{1/3}\left(\frac{g_{s}}{g_{s}^{\mathrm{seed}}}\right)^{1/3}
\]
at any later epoch. Two inputs are not fixed by the formula: $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$, the ceiling of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success} or below it, so that across that range the floor spans a factor $(3.5 \times 10^{11}/6 \times 10^{14})^{3/4}$, about $4 \times 10^{-3}$ ($3.75 \times 10^{-3}$), the body quoting the top and saying so; and the deposit's energy, which sets the actual ratio above the floor.
proof:
With $dt = -dT/(HT)$,
\[
H \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{\pi^{2}g_{*}}{90}}\;\frac{T^{2}}{M_{P}}, \qquad s \;=\; \frac{2\pi^{2}}{45}\,g_{s}T^{3},
\]
in the reduced-mass convention the rate is quoted in (the familiar $1.66\sqrt{g_{*}}\,T^{2}/M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ with the non-reduced $M_{\mathrm{Pl}} = 1.22 \times 10^{19}$ GeV is the same rate, $1.66 = \sqrt{8\pi}\sqrt{\pi^{2}/90}$), the Boltzmann equation $\dot{n} + 3Hn = \Gamma$, gravitational production being the only source (by \claimref{dark-matter.superselected-hence-dark-exactly-stable}), for the comoving yield $Y = n/s$ reads
\[
\frac{dY}{dT} \;=\; -\frac{\Gamma}{HTs} \;=\; -\frac{c\,T^{2}}{\kappa_{s}M_{P}^{3}},
\]
which integrates from $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ downward to the stated $Y$, dominated by the top of the range (the script brackets the integral between Riemann sums of that integrand). The energy fraction is $3T\,n/((\pi^{2}/30)g_{*}T^{4}) = 4Y$ for quanta of mean energy $3T$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}$ follows from $\rho_{d} = (\pi^{2}/30)g_{d}\xi^{4}T^{4}$, which presupposes that the produced quanta thermalise within the tower (true for the mirror's content; assumed for a pure-glue tower). The prefactor, referred to the top of the ceiling range of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.ceiling-valued-inherited-success}, is script-evaluated at $c = 0.01, 1, 10$ and at the coefficients of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.coefficients-floors-they-give-what-gravity}, with the two Planck-mass conventions confirmed to give one rate. Level: proved given the imported rate (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}) and the standard thermal history (the expansion law, the entropy density, the mean quantum energy and the degree-of-freedom values, listed in the section ``Machine verification'' as assumed).

title: The coefficients, the floors they give, and what gravity cannot supply
text:
(i) For a five-dimensional tower whose light content is the nine vectors of its $\mathfrak{u}(3)$, eight gluons and the abelian photon, $c = 9 \times 2.3 \times 10^{-3} = 0.021$, $g_{d} = 18$, and $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} = 3.5 \times 10^{-4}$ at the ceiling reheating; whether those are its light species is part of the coupling question of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.no-coupling-rule-odd-towers-follows}, and the value is the floor for that content, not for the tower.

(ii) For the mirror tower, whose content is the Standard Model's (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), the species sum over four real scalars, forty-five Weyl fermions and twelve vectors gives $c = 0.053$ counting the fermions as $22.5$ Dirac species and $0.078$ counting them singly, with $g_{d} = 4 + 45 \times \tfrac{7}{4} + 24 = 106.75$, hence $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}}$ between $2.8$ and $3.2 \times 10^{-4}$ and, with the charge reading of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, $\eta'$ between $19$ and $26$ at the floor; the bracket is the counting ambiguity and is carried as such, and $\eta'$ would fall below one at the floor only for a coefficient above about $4$.

(iii) The produced yield at the ceiling, $Y = 1.8$ to $2.7 \times 10^{-15}$ per unit entropy for the mirror, falls short of the $8.7 \times 10^{-11}$ baryons per unit entropy our baryon number requires by a factor of $3$ to $5 \times 10^{4}$; closing the gap would need $T_{\mathrm{desc}}$ between $1.9$ and $2.2 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, $31.9$ to $36.2$ times the ceiling, where the floor itself would be $4 \times 10^{-3}$, above the charge-domination crossover and equal to the hot-deposit value of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}, as it must be (the same energy per unit of baryon number either way). Gravity heats the dark towers; it does not populate them with charge, which is the descent's.

(iv) The mirror's contribution to $\Neff$, $7.447\,\xi^{4}$, is below $10^{-13}$ at the floor and below $10^{-8}$ at the hot deposit of Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.stored-asymmetry-charge-not-number}; a nine-vector tower's, $2.202 \times 18\,\xi^{4}$ for eighteen light polarisations, the coefficient being half the two-polarisation $\Delta\Neff$ bracketed in Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.radiation-audit-what-theorem-closes-what}, is below $10^{-12}$ at its floor.
proof: Arithmetic on Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.seeding-gravity-floor-dark-towers-temperature} and Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-massless-graviton-production-rate}, script-bracketed, with $g_{d}$ counting two polarisations per vector, one per real scalar and $\tfrac{7}{8} \times 2$ per Weyl fermion; the species summed in (ii) are the mirror's Standard Model content (by \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), and the counting ambiguity there is whether the imported fermion coefficient is per Weyl or per Dirac species, and the bracket spans both. (iii): $\eta$ times the photon-to-entropy ratio $n_{\gamma}/s = 0.1413$ against $Y$; the temperature that would make up the shortfall inverts $Y \propto T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3}$; the floor at that temperature is $\xi_{\mathrm{floor}} \propto T_{\mathrm{desc}}^{3/4}$, and its agreement with the hot-deposit value is the identity $4Y\,g_{*}/g_{d}$ evaluated at $Y = n_{B}/s$ on both sides. (iv): $g_{r}$ light polarisations at $2.2018$ each, Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.open-channels-their-costs}.

title: No coupling rule for the odd towers follows from the series
text: No rule relating an odd tower's gauge coupling to this tower's follows from the series' premises and theorems, for three independent reasons. (a) In a tower of dimension $d \neq 4$ the gauge coupling is dimensionful, $[g^{2}] = \mathrm{mass}^{4-d}$, so a comparison with this tower's dimensionless coupling needs a length, and in five dimensions that length is the size of the fifth direction, which the sheaf paper's wall construction does not fix \cite{ButlerT4}. (b) No gauge coupling value is derived anywhere in the series (the Standard-Model paper takes $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ from the record \cite[Fact 2.8, Prop.~6.1]{ButlerT12}), so a rule for a dark tower's coupling would be a rule for ours first. (c) Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} cannot supply democracy: the odd towers are inequivalent to this one as soldered algebras (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one}), off the reversal orbit along which alone the audit equates (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv)). Any rule is therefore a premise, and the paper adopts none; structural level, not proved in the sense of \cite{ButlerT1}.
proof: (a): under $g \mapsto \lambda^{2}g$ the volume form scales as $\lambda^{d}$ and the two inverse metrics in $\star$ on two-forms as $\lambda^{-4}$, so $\int F \wedge \star F$ scales as $\lambda^{d-4}$ and $1/g^{2}$ carries the compensating dimension. (b) and (c) are as stated, (c) resting on \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}, which equates along the reversal orbit only, on Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.residue-soldered-invariant-not-algebraic-one} for the inequivalence and on Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}(iv) for the reversal orbit.

Let $W \subset V_\C$ be a maximal totally isotropic subspace ($\dim_\C W = 3$) and $W'$ a complementary maximal isotropic subspace, dual to $W$ under the $\C$-bilinear form (such a pair exists, and any two such pairs are conjugate under $O(V_\C)$). On the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W$ ($\dim_\C = 2^3 = 8$) define
\[
c(w) := \sqrt2\; w \wedge (\cdot) \quad (w \in W),
\qquad
c(w') := \sqrt2\; \iota_{w'} \quad (w' \in W'),
\]
with $\iota$ contraction through the pairing. Then $c(u)^2 = Q(u)\,\id$ for every $u \in W \oplus W' = V_\C$, so $c$ extends to an algebra map $\Cl(V_\C) \to \End(\Lambda^\bullet W)$; this map is an isomorphism, and $\Lambda^\bullet W$ is the unique irreducible module of $\Cl(2,4)_\C$: the Dirac spinors of the completion. \[
\CS := \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}} W, \qquad \CSm := \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}} W,
\]

text: In the current-algebra description of the boundary modes (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}) let $\varphi$ be a state invariant under the $U(1)$ gauge group of the currents, under charge conjugation $C$ ($J \mapsto -J$, $T \mapsto T$), and under the modular flow generated by the zero mode $L_0$ of the Sugawara stress tensor $T$: the conformal vacuum is such a state, and so is the induced state of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} under premise (Q), with charge conjugation implemented on the mode array $\psi_k$ (the fermion modes of the singularity paper's array, Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}) as the particle-hole reflection about the sea level, $C\psi_kC^{-1} = \psi^\dagger_{-k}$, so that $J \mapsto -J$ and $T \mapsto T$; the proof shows that this state has the three invariances, and the proposition is conditional on (Q) wherever it is applied to it. Let $O$ be a probe that is gauge-charged (a fermion field, a condensate order parameter, any operator of nonzero $U(1)$ charge) or neutral and $C$-odd (the charge and spin currents), or, more generally, that lies in a nontrivial irreducible representation of any symmetry of the algebra that $\varphi$ respects and $T$ is invariant under. Then the linear susceptibility of the graviton mode to $O$ vanishes identically: $\varphi(T\,O) = 0$, and likewise for every mode $T_n$. At first order, nothing couples to the pair correlations except the $C$-even neutral subalgebra; in the conformal vacuum that subalgebra's overlap with $T$ is carried by $T$ alone, while in the thermal state it is the whole $C$-even neutral subalgebra, generated by the current bilinears and strictly larger than the conformal family of $T$, that can couple. In the conformal vacuum the statement is strengthened by Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-conformal-orthogonality-sugawara-construction}: every quasi-primary of dimension other than two is orthogonal to $T$ as well, so the only quasi-primary with nonzero overlap is $T$. The equivalence principle thereby acquires its converse at this level: fields differ in how strongly they couple, and the reduced theory proves there is no other channel through which to couple. \emph{Level:} the orthogonality is proved below for any state with the stated invariances; that the induced state of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra} has them is proved in the proof from premise (Q), and is conditional on (Q); that the thermal $C$-even neutral subalgebra is strictly larger than the conformal family of $T$ is a remark, not used.

title: The conclusion does not depend on the ontology, at its level
text: The gravitational-engineering conclusion, that the metric-forming structure admits exactly one coupling sector (stress-energy), with no selective coupling, no enhanced source and no enhanced detector at first order, holds on either reading of the graviton's ontology, with a different level on each. If the graviton is the framework's collective mode: by derivation, Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} and \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} at proof level within the s-wave sector and Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised} for the lift. If the graviton is fundamental: by Weinberg's soft theorem \cite{Weinberg1964}, the leading low-energy coupling of any massless spin-two particle is universal, which is the equivalence principle and rules out a selective coupling at leading order; non-minimal couplings, subleading in energy, are not excluded by the theorem, so the fundamental branch delivers the conclusion at leading order only. The conclusion is therefore common ground between the ontologies at leading order; what is distinctive to the composite reading is the ultraviolet behaviour (quantisation as output; no graviton loops to renormalise), the derivation of weakness as dimensional suppression (Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.weakness-dimension-nonlinear-bound-open-items}), and the $\ell_P^2/A$ corrections carried by the spectrum paper; the discriminating experiments, if any, lie in those corrections, and the asymmetry (hard to refute, hard to confirm below the Planck scale) is stated rather than hidden. title: The four alternatives are exhaustive; the three are not
text: Every conserved $q$ is (D), (P) or (I), and exactly one of them; (K) can hold together with any of them and is excluded by none; (D) implies (K), while (P) and (I) are compatible with (K) and with its negation. The lift inherits the no-go, with its steps itemised
text:
The remaining open item, that the four-dimensional lift might introduce a coupling invisible to the s-wave sector, is addressed by covering the spacetime in two pieces, with one step upgraded. The steps, each with its provenance:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Partial waves (exact, kinematic).} Near the horizon the four-dimensional two-point function between the graviton mode and any probe decomposes over partial waves, and the angular integration is diagonal in $\ell$ by spherical-harmonic orthogonality.
\item \emph{Near-horizon reduction (assembly, at the level it carries in T5).} Each fixed-$\ell$ sector reduces, at the horizon where the potential barrier vanishes, to a two-dimensional copy of the setting of the current algebra, in which the $\ell$-th component of the graviton mode is the $\ell$-th $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-harmonic of the current bilinears. Which operator is the stress tensor in the $\ell$-th copy is fixed by step (4), not assumed.
\item \emph{Exterior exactness (imported theorem).} On any region where the gauge-theoretic metric is invertible, the horizon included, the description coincides exactly with classical general relativity, by the geometry paper's import of gauge-theory gravity from Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite[Fact~2.1]{ButlerT6}, whose couplings to the metric are stress-energy alone. The two pieces overlap and cover the spacetime.
\item \emph{The sphere step (conditional on the entropy paper's Indifference premise; then proved by covariance).} By the sphere theorem (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}, \cite[Thm.~5.5]{ButlerT8}, conditional on \cite[Principle~5.4]{ButlerT8}) every angular operator of the lift is a boundary-mode bilinear of definite spin under the adjoint $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, of spin $\ell \geq 1$ for every non-trivial harmonic, while the s-wave stress tensor $T$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ singlet. In an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-invariant state the symmetry orthogonality of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} applies verbatim: nonzero spin, zero overlap. Orthogonality by dimension would \emph{not} do here, the bilinears having dimension two like $T$; it is the spin that separates them. The lift inherits the no-go because the sphere is built from the same correlations to which the no-go applies, and those correlations carry spin.
\end{enumerate}
With Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.acoustic-no-go-one-way-grip} and \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} and these steps, the acoustic programme is closed at the mixed level of its inputs: the metric-forming correlations admit exactly one coupling sector, its weakness is dimensional, its leading nonlinearity is Gertsenshtein's, and its Goldstones are eaten. Step (2), the near-horizon reduction, is at assembly level, its promotion shared with T5 and T7; step (4) is conditional on the entropy paper's Indifference premise, and the closure of the acoustic programme inherits that condition.

text:

Classification of the real Clifford algebras
text: Let $d \equiv p - q \pmod 8$. Then $\Cl(p,q)$ is isomorphic, as a real associative algebra, to the entry of the table of the section ``The mod-8 classification'': $\Mat_k(\R)$ for $d \in \{0, 2\}$, $\Mat_k(\C)$ for $d \in \{3, 7\}$, $\Mat_k(\HH)$ for $d \in \{4, 6\}$, $\Mat_k(\R) \oplus \Mat_k(\R)$ for $d = 1$, and $\Mat_k(\HH) \oplus \Mat_k(\HH)$ for $d = 5$, with $k$ fixed in each case by $\dim_\R \Cl(p,q) = 2^n$. In particular $\Cl(p,q)$ is simple except when $p - q \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, where it is the direct sum of two isomorphic simple algebras.

title: The infinite wall sequence
text: Let $\Sig$ be compact. For good couplings at every stage, there is an infinite sequence $\Sig = \Sig^{(0)}, \Sig^{(1)} = \Sig', \Sig^{(2)}, \dots$ of tame walls, each displaced from the last into the unphysical region, carrying Clifford sheaves of ranks $2^n, 2^{n+2}, 2^{n+4}, \dots$ whose physical-side fibres ascend the Witt tower $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1) \to \Cl(p{+}2,q{+}2) \to \cdots$, one Rule-1 rung per wall. Degeneracy is conserved along the entire sequence: each completion resolves its wall and produces the next, displaced successively further from the physical region.
