title: Chirality: the two halves of the spinor module, and conjugation as duality
text: The conformal spinor space $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ (twistor space) and its partner $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves of the ascended Dirac module (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the sector of a single conformal spinor $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ is their direct sum. Under $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ the two halves carry different content: $\CS$ carries $(1)_{0} \oplus (\bar{3})_{-2/3}$ and $\CSm{}$ carries $(3)_{-1/3} \oplus (1)_{-1}$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3)), so the two halves are inequivalent representations of the group: the chirality split is visible to the internal symmetry, not only to the grading. The singlet spectrum listed by a single handedness is Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(2)'s, and in particular the colour content $3 \oplus \bar{3}$ of the two halves becomes $\bar{3} \oplus \bar{3}$ under it, which is the conjugation of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.weakness-examined-exotics-conjugation-hypercharge}. Moreover the conjugation is an operation inside the pair system: the dual of the grade-$k$ state is the grade-$(3-k)$ state with the full-system phase removed, $(\Lambda^{k}W)^{*} \cong \Lambda^{3-k}W \otimes (\Lambda^{3}W)^{*}$, of weight $+2k$; and the two doublets at the level of one conformal spinor of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(2) are each other's duals, $(\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{0}W)^{*} \cong \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{3}W$, and under (S) have opposite parity. Under (S) they are therefore one doublet and its antiparticle, not two candidates, and Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency}(1)'s listing choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation of Remark \claimref{note.standard-model.weakness-examined-exotics-conjugation-hypercharge}.

title: Four dimensions from the forces, and the converse
text:
(1) Let the spacetime dimension $n$ be even, and suppose that in dimension $n$, as in dimension four (Fact \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula}), a single conformal spinor (twistor) is massless and mass first exists at two constituents. Then the pair count per conformal spinor is $(n+2)/2$ (Lemma \claimref{standard-model.pair-count-dimension}), the minimal massive hierarchy is $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{(n+2)/2}$, and its automorphism algebra is $\su(2) \oplus \su((n+2)/2) \oplus \uu(1)$ by the argument of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}, which for $m \neq k$ uses the Segre lemma and the tensor factorisation only, and which at $n = 2$, where $m = k = 2$, still applies because an automorphism is defined as a map of the form $A \otimes B$, so that the swap of factors is excluded by definition, as in (2). This equals the Standard Model algebra if and only if $n = 4$. If, therefore, the gauge algebra of matter is the automorphism algebra of its minimal massive compositeness, four dimensions is a consequence: four is the dimension in which the pair count is three. The identification premise is Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}'s reading, the mass-begins-at-two hypothesis in dimension $n \neq 4$ is a hypothesis (the mass paper proves it in dimension four only), and both conditionalities are declared.

(2) Conversely, with no hypothesis on $n$: for every two-factor hierarchy $\C^{m} \otimes \C^{k}$ with $m, k \ge 1$ the automorphism algebra is $\su(m) \oplus \su(k) \oplus \uu(1)$, of dimension $m^{2} + k^{2} - 1$, and it is isomorphic to the Standard Model algebra if and only if $\{m, k\} = \{2, 3\}$ as an unordered pair. So the gauge algebra, once identified, forces the hierarchy to be a two-by-three, and one further input orders it: given that mass begins at two constituents ($m = 2$), the pair count is three, hence four dimensions by Lemma \claimref{standard-model.pair-count-dimension}; given four dimensions ($k = 3$), the constituents number two. Under Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}'s reading, each of the two framework inputs is a consequence of the observed forces together with the other, not only consistent with them; the algebra alone does not distinguish two conformal spinors of three pairs from three of two.

title: Hypothesis (S): slot statistics, derived from the slot-module hypothesis
text:
\emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} Under the slot-module hypothesis (Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}: the composite space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that is the grading of the joint Clifford system once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Odd slots.)} If the slot quanta are tower elements of one tower parity $\pi$ whose tower grading $(-1)^{\pi n + k}$ is the chirality, then $\pi = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Slot content.)} $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, so the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W = \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; its particle half is $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Chirality.)} As in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exclusion statistics.)} Every $U(2)$-equivariant slot creation map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ satisfies $a^{\dagger}(u)a^{\dagger}(u') = -a^{\dagger}(u')a^{\dagger}(u)$ for all $u, u' \in \C^{2}$; in particular $a^{\dagger}(u)^{2} = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} The slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs: the two slot modes and the three pair modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations as one system of five modes, so that, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}, their Majorana combinations generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, its spinor module, whose parity grading is that module's chirality.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (ii) and (iv) are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) under the premise's generation clause and CPT halving, with no anomaly condition; (v) is the premise's clause (f), applied once (ii) has made the slot module fermionic; (iii) follows from the premise's requirement that the chirality be the grading of the joint Clifford system, which makes it commute with $\Spin(10)$; (i) compares (iii) with a tower grading. The particle half satisfies the four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, a consequence here and not a premise.
provenance: Transport Lab claim standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics, version 8 (T12 Hypothesis (S))

title: Imported: the Fock representation of a Clifford algebra, and its Bogoliubov group
text: Let $E$ be a complex vector space of dimension $n$ with a Hermitian inner product, and let $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ be the Fock space of $n$ fermionic modes, with creation operators the exterior multiplications and annihilation operators the contractions. The $2n$ Majorana combinations of these operators generate an action of the complex Clifford algebra of a $2n$-dimensional orthogonal space on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$, which is its irreducible spinor module; the parity grading $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}} \oplus \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}$ is the chirality decomposition into the two half-spinor modules. The orthogonal transformations of the Majorana generators preserve the canonical anticommutation relations and are implemented on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ by the group $\mathrm{Pin}(2n)$, the connected component $SO(2n)$ by $\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$, which acts on each half-spinor module irreducibly for $n \ge 2$; the transformations preserving the complex structure of $E$, equivalently the mode number, form $U(n) \subset SO(2n)$, acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(g)$ up to a determinant phase. For $n = 3$ this is the structure of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}; for $n = 5$ it is $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ with $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lecture~20, \S 20.1]{FultonHarris1991} for the spinor module as an exterior algebra and its half-spin decomposition; \cite[Ch.~I, \S\S 2, 5]{LawsonMichelsohn1989} for $\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$ as the double cover of $SO(2n)$ and its spin representation; the Fock-space form is the standard second-quantised reading of the same construction.
provenance: W. Fulton and J. Harris, Representation Theory: A First Course, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 129, Springer (1991)., Lecture~20, \S 20.1; H. B. Lawson and M.-L. Michelsohn, Spin Geometry, Princeton University Press (1989)., Ch.~I, \S\S 2, 5

title: The trichotomy: what kind of number $N$ is
text:
The question the paper ends by pointing at can itself be classified. The classification has four parts, of which the first contains a proved statement and a reading, the second is an import, the third is conditional on the first two, on Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent} and on a decision the fourth names, and the fourth is imported from the action paper; the levels are marked clause by clause.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Kinematic.)} Proved: under $\Lambda \to s^{2}\Lambda$ at fixed $M_{P}$, that is $I \to sI$ on the frozen point with the conformal class unchanged, $H \to sH$ and $N \to N/s$, while every discrete invariant this paper derives (the algebra and its dimension twelve, the global form and its $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$, the dimension four, the content and the hypercharges, and under (S) the ratio $3/8$) is unchanged, since each is computed from the conformal class, the pair structure and the group alone, none of which the rescaling affects. Reading, at observation level: since the conformal class and the pair structure carry no scale, no construction from them alone can fix $N$, which lies in the ratio of the frozen point's norm to the Planck scale; on this reading the kinematic layer determines all discrete invariants and no continuous modulus, and $N$ and the weight spectrum are its only continuous moduli.
\item \emph{(Non-dynamical, imported.)} $\Lambda$ is the norm of the frozen point, and the norm is not a field: it is fixed by a constraint, the fluctuations of the frozen point are pure gauge, and the action carries no equation of motion for it (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-norm-frozen-point-not-field}).
\item \emph{(Initial data, conditional.)} If the alternatives kinematic, dynamical and initial-data are exhaustive, then by (1) and (2) $N$ is initial data, and Observation \claimref{standard-model.dating-descent}(ii) locates the boundary that carries it at the origin. The exhaustiveness is not proved here, and the location is an Observation; the clause is conditional on both, and clause (4) says what the exhaustiveness costs.
\item \emph{(Parameter of the laws, imported.)} The three alternatives are not exhaustive: a conserved quantity that is constant on every solution of a theory but varies across a family of theories indexed by a parameter is a parameter of the laws, and the action paper proves that under the action as written, with $\Lambda$ the value of the Stelle-West constraints fixed before variation, $N$ is exactly that: constant on each solution space $\mathcal{S}_{\Lambda}$ by the rigidity of (2), varying across $\Lambda$, so neither dynamically fixed nor initial data \cite[Prop.~5.8]{ButlerT10}. Clause (3) therefore holds only if the norm is promoted from a fixed number to the value of a Lagrange-multiplier field whose constancy is an equation of motion, the Henneaux-Teitelboim mechanism, which makes $\Lambda$ a label of the solution rather than of the theory; that promotion is a decision for the series, recorded open with both branches stated \cite[Rem.~5.9]{ButlerT10}, and the entropic and null-endpoint effects named below act on a measure over theories or on a measure within one theory according to it.
\end{enumerate}
At observation level, two competing effects are then named without being balanced: an entropic weighting of the freezing by $\exp(S_{\Lambda}) = \exp(\pi N^{2})$, with $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ the cosmological horizon's area-law entropy (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}), favours large $N$ overwhelmingly (the well-known entropic argument for small $\Lambda$, inherited with every one of its known objections, listed as inherited and not solved), while at the endpoint $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is null and the curvature-squared presentation of the action, whose prefactor is $3/\Lambda$, does not exist; the action paper is explicit that this is a boundary of the presentation and not of the action, the Einstein-Cartan functional remaining \cite[Thm.~3.1, Rem.~3.2]{ButlerT10}, so what is lost at $\Lambda = 0$ is the reductive structure and the frozen point's length, not gravity. Large because large boundary mode spaces dominate the measure; nonzero because the descent selects a frozen point of nonzero length; the value is the balance point, and the balance point awaits the descent measure, the one object this framework does not possess. Last, a statement of units only, flagged as such: in the boundary modes' own units, qubits, one per rung of the Fock module (Theorem \claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}), the horizon's capacity $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ is $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, about $4.8 \times 10^{122}$ qubits (the mode count of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-mode-count} under the black hole's counting rule), whose base-two logarithm is about $407$; the paper's $R = \log_{2} N^{2} \approx 405$ counts the rungs of a module of dimension $N^{2}$, whose capacity is only $\ln N^{2} = 2\ln N$ nats, not the horizon's. Neither number is a count of turns of the mod-8 clock, which no rung moves: each rung preserves the residue $p - q \pmod 8$ (Theorem \claimref{transport.rule-1-morita-trivial}). This is the question in the framework's own coordinates, not an answer to it.

title: Isometries extend to algebra homomorphisms
text: An isometry $f : (V, Q) \to (W, Q')$ extends to a unique unital algebra homomorphism $\Cl(f) : \Cl(V, Q) \to \Cl(W, Q')$ with $\Cl(f)(v) = f(v)$. It is injective when $f$ is, and $\Cl(g \circ f) = \Cl(g) \circ \Cl(f)$. In particular the orthogonal group $\mathrm{O}(V, Q)$ acts on $\Cl(V, Q)$ by automorphisms, and the inclusion of a subspace $U \subseteq V$ gives an embedding $\Cl(U, Q|_U) \hookrightarrow \Cl(V, Q)$.

title: How the pseudoscalar commutes
Orthogonal bases and the law of inertia
text: Every real quadratic space $(V, Q)$ of dimension $n$ has an orthogonal basis $e_1, \dots, e_n$ with $Q(e_i) \in \{1, -1, 0\}$. The numbers $p$, $q$ and $r$ of basis vectors with $Q(e_i) = 1$, $-1$ and $0$ do not depend on the basis (Sylvester's law of inertia). Moreover $r = \dim \operatorname{rad} V$, and $p + q$ is the rank of any Gram matrix of $B$. Two real quadratic spaces are isometric if and only if they have the same $(p, q, r)$.
provenance: T. Y. Lam, Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields, AMS (2005)., the diagonalisation of forms and Sylvester's law of inertia (real case)

title: Null pairs satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations
Witt's extension theorem
text: Let $(V, Q)$ be a nondegenerate real quadratic space, $U \subseteq V$ any subspace and $f : U \to V$ an injective isometry. Then $f$ extends to an isometry of $V$, that is an element of $\mathrm{O}(V, Q)$. Equivalently (Witt cancellation): if $A \perp B$ and $A' \perp B'$ are nondegenerate with $A \cong A'$ and $A \perp B \cong A' \perp B'$, then $B \cong B'$. Every such extension is a product of reflections $x \mapsto x - 2\frac{B(x, a)}{Q(a)}\, a$, since $V$ is nondegenerate (\claimref{std-algebra.cartan-dieudonne}). The hypothesis that $V$ is nondegenerate cannot be dropped: an isometry of $V$ maps $\operatorname{rad} V$ to itself.
provenance: E. Witt, Theorie der quadratischen Formen in beliebigen Koerpern, J. Reine Angew. Math. 176 (1937)., Satz 4; T. Y. Lam, Introduction to Quadratic Forms over Fields, AMS (2005)., Ch. I (Witt's extension and cancellation theorems)

title: On the conformal ambient, the field action of CPT conjugation is the pseudoscalar rotor times complex conjugation
text:
Let $\R^{2,4}$ carry the conformal ambient metric, $\Cl(2,4)$ its Clifford algebra with $e_0^2 = e_1^2 = 1$ and $e_2^2 = \dots = e_5^2 = -1$, $I_6 = e_0 e_1 \cdots e_5$ its unit pseudoscalar and $\kappa$ complex conjugation on $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C$. Let $W \subset \C^6$ be a maximal isotropic subspace with $W \cap \overline W = 0$ (the generic Witt flag of Definition \claimref{obj.dark-matter.witt-flag}), and $\psi_W$ its pure spinor.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The composite of grade involution and reversal is an anti-automorphism of $\Cl(2,4)$, not an automorphism, and acts on vectors as $-1$. Grade involution equals $\mathrm{Ad}(I_6)$, and $I_6 = (e_0e_1)(e_2e_3)(e_4e_5)$ is a rotor of the identity component: each factor squares to $-1$ and is $\exp(\pi B_k/2)$, and $I_6 \widetilde{I_6} = 1$. So the vector action $-1$ lies in $SO_0(2,4)$. In $\Cl(1,3)$, by contrast, $I_4\widetilde{I_4} = -1$.
\item $W$ is the $+i$ eigenspace of an orthogonal complex structure $J$ on $\R^{2,4}$, $W \oplus \overline W = \C^6$, and $I_6\psi_{W} = \pm i\,\psi_{W}$, $I_6 \psi_{\overline W} = \mp i\,\psi_{\overline W}$. So $\overline W$ lies in the other family, and complex conjugation is a flag conjugate. In $\Cl(3,3)$, $I_6^2 = +1$ and conjugation preserves the family.
\item Every real-linear isometry $g$ of $\R^{2,4}$ with $g(W) = \overline W$ has $\det g = -1$, so that $\epsilon(gI, gV, gF, gF) = -\epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ for vectors $I, V$ and bivectors $F$, $g$ acting on bivectors by its outermorphism. The complex-linear Witt exchange $v_k \leftrightarrow w_k$ does not preserve $\R^{2,4}$.
\item $C := \mathrm{Ad}(I_6) \circ \kappa$ is an antilinear involutive automorphism of $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C$ that is $-1$ on $\R^{2,4}$, fixes the metric, $\epsilon$ and $I_6$, and carries $\psi_W$ to a multiple of $\psi_{\overline W}$. With the flag conjugate realised by $\kappa$, the stored composite $\phi$ (grade involution, reversal, flag conjugate) is reversal composed with $C$: an antilinear anti-automorphism. No realisation of the flag conjugate on $\R^{2,4}$ is both real-linear and orientation-preserving.
\item \emph{Convention.} A (possibly anti-) automorphism $\phi$ acts on fields as a symmetry: on a vector field by its vector part, and on a connection $A$ through the Lie algebra automorphism it induces, $A \mapsto -\phi(A)$ when $\phi$ is an anti-automorphism, so that curvature transforms by the same automorphism; for the stored composite this is the action of $C$. In this convention every action functional of real tensor (multivector) fields on which $C$ acts through its vector part, invariant under constant $SO_0(2,4)$ transformations, in particular the frozen point's $Q(I)^{-1}\int \epsilon(I, V, F, F)$ (\claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}), satisfies $S \circ \phi = S$, while with any real-linear flag conjugate in place of $\kappa$ the same action changes sign. Spinor fields are not covered. If instead $\phi$ is applied to the Clifford integrand $IVFF$ as a whole and the top-grade coefficient taken, both sign statements invert (with $\kappa$ the integrand changes sign, with a real-linear flag conjugate it is preserved), so the conclusion of (5) depends on the convention.
\end{enumerate}

title: The dimmed final burst is the standard burst rescaled in time; its primary high-energy tail is dimmed by the full ratio, its energy in a fixed final window only by the two-thirds power
text:
Let a black hole of the one metric evaporate in the regime where every populated tower's light species are lighter than its temperature, so that the emission coefficients are constant. Write $\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$ for this tower's coefficient in the mass-loss law, $\Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}$ for the gravitational sector's, $\Psi_{\mathrm{odd}}$ for the odd towers', $\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}$ for the total, $g = \Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}/\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$, $o = \Psi_{\mathrm{odd}}/\Psi_{\mathrm{vis}}$, and let the standard expectation be the hole with this tower and gravitons only, total coefficient $\Psi_{0} = \Psi_{\mathrm{vis}} + \Psi_{\mathrm{grav}}$. Put $D = \Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/\Psi_{0}$. Let $\tau$ be the hole's remaining lifetime and $N(E;\tau)$ the number of visible quanta per unit energy emitted in its last $\tau$, $N_{0}$ its standard value.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Every channel's flux per unit energy depends on $M$ and $E$ only through $ME$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.greybody-inheritance-under-interface-premise}), so $dM/dt = -\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}/M^{2}$ and $M(\tau)^{3} = 3\Psi_{\mathrm{tot}}\tau$; at fixed $M$ the visible power is the same as in the standard case (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.parallel-boundary-mode-spaces-one-wall}(i)).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Time rescaling.)} For any visible emission $h(E, M)$ per unit time, secondaries included, the same function in every tower configuration because the exterior metric does not record which tower the mass came from,
\[
N(E;\tau) \;=\; \frac{1}{D}\, N_{0}(E;D\tau):
\]
the visible burst of the last $\tau$ is the standard burst of the last $D\tau$, divided by $D$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Three dimming laws.)} Consequently, at fixed remaining lifetime: the visible energy emitted in the last $\tau$ is $D^{-2/3}$ times its standard value; the hole's temperature is $D^{-1/3}$ times its standard value; and for primary emission, whose flux depends on $E$ and $M$ only through $ME$, the high-energy tail $N(E;\tau) \to C\,E^{-3}/(\Psi_{0}D)$ for $E\,M(\tau)$ large, which does not depend on $\tau$, is $1/D$ times its standard value. Only this primary tail, and the visible fraction of the power at fixed mass, are dimmed by the full ratio.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Floor.)} The mirror's light content copies ours (Theorem \claimref{dark-matter.mirror-tower-copy-one}), so $D = (2 + g + o)/(1 + g) = 2 + (o - g)/(1 + g)$: $D \ge 2$ if and only if $o \ge g$, and with $o = 0$, $D = 2 - g/(1 + g)$. The factors of (iii) are $D$, $D^{2/3}$ and $D^{1/3}$.
\end{enumerate}
The odd towers enter only through $o$; the burst prediction needs their emission coefficients and no other property of them.

title: Commuting copies
text:
Inside $T_k$, let $B_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the $2k$ plane generators $e_1, f_1, \dots, e_k, f_k$, and let $A_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the twisted base generators $x^{(k)} := x\,\omega_1 \omega_2 \cdots \omega_k$ for $x$ among the ground generators. Then: $B_k \cong \Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$; $A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$ via $x \mapsto x^{(k)}$ (the twisted generators satisfy the ground Clifford relations); $A_k$ and $B_k$ commute elementwise; and multiplication $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$ is an isomorphism of algebras,
\[
\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \;=\; \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q)).
\]
The isomorphism is canonical given the ordered planes, and compatible with the tower embeddings up to the twist tracked in the section ``The CAR limit''.
provenance: Transport Lab claim tower.commuting-copies, version 5 (T03 Thm 3.2)

title: Fock module; one qubit per rung
text: Let $W_k := \operatorname{span}\{v_1, \dots, v_k\}$, a maximal isotropic subspace of $H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$. The Chevalley action ($v_j$ by wedge, $w_j$ by contraction against the pairing) makes the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W_k$, of dimension $2^k$, an irreducible module over $B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, with the vacuum $1 \in \Lambda^0$ annihilated by every $w_j$ and cyclic for the $v_j$. Each rung doubles the module: $\Lambda^\bullet W_{k+1} = \Lambda^\bullet W_k \otimes \Lambda^\bullet \R v_{k+1}$, one qubit per rung.
provenance: Transport Lab claim tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung, version 6 (T03 Thm 4.2)

title: Rigidity; the clock is frozen
text: Along the tower: the transport charge $d = p - q \bmod 8$ is constant; the division-ring type, simplicity class, and centre of every floor equal those of the ground floor; every floor is Morita equivalent to the ground floor; and the obstruction taxonomy of \cite{ButlerT1} is floor-independent: in particular a type-C obstruction (a central idempotent) never arises by transport from a simple ground algebra, at any height. The physical tower is $\Cl(1{+}k, 3{+}k) \cong \Mat_{2^{k+1}}(\HH)$, frozen at clock position $6$. Bott periodicity manifests as immediate freeze, not eventual return.
provenance: Transport Lab claim tower.rigidity-clock-frozen, version 5 (T03 Thm 3.6)

title: Witt index is quantum capacity
text: For any nondegenerate real quadratic space $(V, Q)$, the maximal number of pairwise-anticommuting fermionic mode pairs realisable by \emph{vectors} of $\Cl(V, Q)$ (families $(a_i, b_i)$ of vectors satisfying the displayed CAR of Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) is exactly the Witt index $\min(p,q)$ of $Q$. Along the tower the Witt index is $\min(p,q) + k$: each rung raises the algebra's mode capacity by exactly one, and by no more.
provenance: Transport Lab claim tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity, version 4 (T03 Thm 4.3)

title: A pre-descent $\theta$-term sources the matter asymmetry
text: The refuted claim is that a $\theta$-term present before the descent sources the matter asymmetry through the topology of gauge bundles. A $\theta$-term integrates a characteristic class of even degree, so the odd-dimensional towers carry no continuous $\theta$. In this tower a non-relaxing angle of order one at the descent is excluded by the neutron electric dipole bound, which gives $|\theta| \lesssim 10^{-10}$ today; an angle that relaxes or rolls is not excluded. The framework instead inherits its asymmetry as initial data, the Witt flag being the one mechanism it supplies itself.

title: The particle-antiparticle orientation is determined by the charge-zero condition
text: The refuted expectation is that the charge-zero condition fixes the one absolute bit the Standard-Model derivation left open, the particle-antiparticle orientation. A $\Z_{2}$ covariance argument on three premises (CPT conjugation is an isomorphism of every kinematic structure, Hypothesis (S), and, for the last step, the trichotomy's exhaustiveness) shows that whatever the structures determine is conjugation-invariant, while the orientation is not. The charge-zero condition fixes all relative structure; the absolute bit is initial data, and it is the Witt flag, the same choice as the arrow of time.
